events.title: Human Creativity Festival
events.description: The Beaver County Green Party will present Human Creativity: A Festival for Arts & Environment on Sunday, October 4, 2026 at PJ Caul Memorial Park in Ambridge, PA.An all day, family-friendly event, Human Creativity is dedicated to calling attention to the negative impacts that data centers and artificial intelligence are having on traditional artisans and the environment in our region. The festival will feature music performances by regional acts Nowhere Wolves, Crisp Lake, Mean Blue Planets, Jack McNally, The Stolen Stitches, Jack Hell and more. Over 20 vendors will be in attendance - ranging from zine creators to candlemakers to potters and crochet hookers. Many artisans will also conduct demos and workshops throughout the event. All festival participants pledge to keep their art free from artificial intelligence.Local eats will be available throughout the event by Savory Station and Highland Homestead Farm food trucks.Human Creativity: A Festival for Arts & Environment will take place from 11am to 8pm on Sunday, October 4. Vendors and/or volunteers who may be interested in participating in the festival, please contact Lorianne Burgess at 724-419-6632 or stanglsbakery@gmail.com

events.title: Off the Altar: Ceramics Workshop
events.description: Be a part of the process during this engaging workshop with artist and professor Britney Smith. Rooted in hand-building practices, Smith creates ceramic vessels that illustrate what is held, tended, and carried forward; documenting her lineage and intergenerational wisdom in clay. Her subtly marked surfaces are uniquely textured with soda-firing, an unpredictable and time-intensive atmospheric firing process mirroring the quiet labor of inheritance. Drawing on legacies within her family, Smith connects the symbolic language of Black foodways through everyday objects, dedicating her domestic wares as sites of remembrance.

events.title: An Afternoon in Paris: Silent Film with Live Music
events.description: Step into the playful spirit of Jazz Age Paris with a special silent film presentation inspired by the French Moderns: Matisse / Renoir / Degas exhibition. Join us for Ernst Lubitsch’s stylish 1926 comedy So This Is Paris, a witty tale of romance, intrigue, and modern city life, featuring one of silent cinema’s most celebrated dance sequences. The film comes to life through live musical accompaniment by Tom Roberts, jazz pianist, composer, and music historian, capturing the vibrant spirit of early moviegoing. Presented as part of the annual Pittsburgh Silent Film Festival with commentary by festival director Chad Hunter, this special afternoon celebrates the magic of silent cinema through the dynamic partnership of film and live music. Film runtime: Approx. 1 hour 10 minutes, followed by Q&A. Gallery access is not included with the program. We encourage guests to purchase tickets to French Moderns: Matisse / Renoir / Degas for viewing before or after the program. Advance registration and pre-payment are recommended; walk-ups will be accommodated as space allows.

events.title: Benjamin Tod and The Inline Six
events.description: Benjamin Tod and The Lost Dog Street Band are known for raw, emotionally honest songwriting rooted in folk, country, and Americana traditions. Benjamin Tod’s music explores themes of addiction, poverty, heartbreak, redemption, and life on the fringes of society through deeply personal lyrics and stripped-down acoustic arrangements. His gritty vocal style and unfiltered storytelling have earned a devoted following among fans of outlaw country and modern folk music. Known for intimate and emotionally powerful performances, Benjamin Tod delivers songs that balance vulnerability with rugged authenticity.The Inline Six brings a roots-driven sound shaped by country, Americana, and folk influences, emphasizing heartfelt songwriting and organic musicianship. Their performances combine traditional acoustic textures with emotionally grounded storytelling that reflects working-class experiences, relationships, and life on the road. With a warm and authentic live presence, the group complements Benjamin Tod’s introspective style while contributing to a deeply personal and Americana-focused concert atmosphere.

events.description: Foster the People is an indie pop and alternative rock band known for infectious melodies, danceable rhythms, and a colorful sound that blends pop, electronic, and psychedelic influences. The group gained international attention through catchy, upbeat songs paired with thoughtful lyrics that often explore social issues, youth culture, and emotional complexity beneath their energetic sound. Their music combines shimmering synths, groovy bass lines, and layered production into a style that feels both modern and nostalgic. Known for vibrant live performances and genre-crossing creativity, Foster the People has remained a standout act in contemporary indie and alternative music.

events.title: Stryper
events.description: Stryper is a pioneering Christian hard rock band known for its distinctive “heavenly metal” style, yellow-and-black visual identity, tight vocal harmonies, melodic guitar work and faith-centered lyrics. Formed in Southern California in 1983, the group broke into the mainstream with the multiplatinum 1986 album To Hell with the Devil. Its best-known songs include “Calling on You,” “Honestly” and “Always There for You,” while the band has sold more than 10 million albums worldwide. Stryper’s current lineup features founding members Michael Sweet, Robert Sweet and Oz Fox, alongside bassist Perry Richardson.

Her performances often explore topics such as mental health, family dynamics, social anxiety, and everyday awkwardness through eccentric characters, unexpected voices, and sharp observational wit. Bamford has earned widespread acclaim for blending vulnerability with absurdist comedy, creating a unique comedic voice that stands apart in modern stand-up entertainment. With acclaimed specials, television appearances, and an inventive approach to live performance, Maria Bamford remains one of the most distinctive and influential comedians working today.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM--FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.title: Ten Evenings: Mary Roach
events.description: The body is the most complex machine in the world, and the only one for which you cannot get a replacement part from the manufacturer. For centuries, medicine has reached for what’s available—sculpting noses from brass, borrowing skin from frogs and hearts from pigs, crafting eye parts from jet canopies and breasts from petroleum by-products. Today we’re attempting to grow body parts from scratch using stem cells and 3D printers. How are we doing? Are we there yet?In Replaceable You, Mary Roach explores the remarkable advances and difficult questions prompted by the human body’s failings. When and how does a person decide they’d be better off with a prosthetic than their existing limb? Can a donated heart be made to beat forever? Can an intestine provide a workable substitute for a vagina?Roach dives in with her characteristic verve and infectious wit. Her travels take her to the OR at a legendary burn unit in Boston, a “superclean” xeno-pigsty in China, and a stem cell “hair nursery” in the San Diego tech hub. She talks with researchers and surgeons, amputees and ostomates, printers of kidneys and designers of wearable organs. She spends time in a working iron lung from the 1950s, stays up all night with recovery techs as they disassemble and reassemble a tissue donor, and travels across Mongolia with the cataract surgeons of Orbis International.Irrepressible and accessible, Replaceable You immerses readers in the wondrous, improbable, and surreal quest to build a new you.Mary Roach is the author of the New York Times bestsellers STIFF, SPOOK, BONK, GULP, GRUNT, FUZZ, and PACKING FOR MARS. Her new book, REPLACEABLE YOU: Adventures in Human Anatomy, debuts in September 2025. Mary has written for National Geographic, Wired, and The New York Times Magazine, among others, and her TED talk made the TED 20 Most Watched list. She has been a guest editor for Best American Science and Nature Writing, a finalist for the Royal Society’s Winton Prize, and a winner of the American Engineering Societies’ journalism award, in a category for which, let’s be honest, she was the sole entrant. More at www.maryroach.net

events.description: Medium Build is the musical project of singer-songwriter Nick Carpenter, an Alaska-based artist known for emotionally candid indie pop that draws from pop, country and singer-songwriter traditions. His autobiographical writing explores identity, vulnerability and recovery, with a sound that balances intimate confession and expansive melody. Notable releases include the album Country, the EP Health, and songs such as “Crying Over U,” “Rage” and “In My Room.” Medium Build has also collaborated with X Ambassadors vocalist Sam Harris on “Friend for Life,” which reached the Top 20 of Billboard’s Alternative Digital Song Sales chart.

events.title: Spinning 1 Series with Jasmine (Min) Davis
events.description: Learn how to use a drop spindle and a spinning wheel to create your own yarn for knitting, crocheting, weaving, and/or admiring!!! Spinning 1 Series with Jasmine (Min) Davis 6-Part Series Workshop! Date: Tuesdays, October 6 – November 17 (no class meeting on October 27) 6-9pm Description: Whether you dream of owning a flock of sheep someday or you want to join your local reenactors guilds—or anywhere in between!—spinning yarn is a skill that’s useful in a variety of situations. In this introductory class, students will learn how to use a drop spindle and a spinning wheel to create their own yarn for knitting, crocheting, weaving, and/or admiring. Over the course of six weeks, students will learn about two common tools for spinning yarn: drop spindles and spinning wheels. You’ll come away with two or more finished skeins of your own handspun yarn and the foundational skills you’ll need to continue building your spinning practice. PLEASE NOTE: Corriedale sheep wool is used for this class. If you have an allergy or prefer not to use animal fiber, please contact Senior Education Manager, Jamie Boyle by leaving a message at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org to discuss accommodations. Tuition: $270 + $30 materials fee Materials: Materials fee includes fiber and drop spindles. Students can use the spinning wheels in studio. Registration: Register via Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing on the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Fill out the scholarship application here. You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions about scholarships, email Jamie Boyle at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. We strive to create a welcoming experience. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the artist: Jasmine Davis (Min) (she/her) is a fiber artist in Pittsburgh, PA . She enjoys spinning (yarn), spinning (poi), and spinning (in circles). She loves exploring color and texture across various textile mediums, and helping students discover possibilities within their materials.

events.title: Robert Ellis
events.description: Robert Ellis is a critically acclaimed singer-songwriter, guitarist, and multi-instrumentalist whose sophisticated blend of Americana, country, folk, jazz, and rock has earned him widespread respect as one of today's most versatile musicians. A native of Texas, Ellis is celebrated for his exceptional songwriting, expressive guitar playing, and willingness to explore a wide range of musical styles while remaining rooted in honest, character-driven storytelling. His acclaimed albums, including The Lights from the Chemical Plant, Robert Ellis, Texas Piano Man, and Yesterday's News, showcase lyrical depth, melodic craftsmanship, and arrangements that seamlessly balance traditional influences with contemporary creativity. Onstage, Ellis captivates audiences with his warm vocals, understated charisma, and remarkable musicianship, whether performing intimate acoustic sets or full-band concerts. Through thoughtful songwriting, genre-defying artistry, and an unwavering commitment to musical excellence, Robert Ellis has established himself as one of the most compelling and respected voices in modern Americana.

events.description: It’s time to focus on your liver health education: 35% of Americans incorrectly believe you can live without a liver! Welcome to MASH Across America, a disease education initiative designed to bring liver health education directly to communities across the country with a giant 40-foot inflatable liver. We’re coming to Pittsburgh to spark new conversations about the critical role the liver plays in our overall health and shine a light on a disease many people don’t see coming: fatty liver disease. Join us on Wednesday, October 7th from 2:00-6:00 pm ET in the Tailgate Zone at F.N.B. Stadium for a day of educational fun! The event is free and open to the public. Learn more about MASH Across America and the cities we’ve visited here: https://mashacrossamerica.com/.

events.title: Turning Night! Guided Open Studio with Matt Iannacci
events.description: Open to anyone who's tried their hand at woodturning, come spend the evening making your latest project under Matt's guidance! 3-Hour Guided Open Studio Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 Time: 6–9pm Description: Spend the evening on the lathes with fellow turners! Join us for Turning Night, a guided open studio session open to anyone who’s taken a woodturning workshop with us before—or anyone with experience on a wood lathe at all! Come with a project idea and Matt will guide you through the setup and technique to make it happen. This is the perfect opportunity for anyone with some turning experience to pursue their own project—but in the presence of an experienced woodturning instructor! The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, including pen blanks ( pen kit available here ), spindle blanks, and bowl blanks. However, for a more specific project, students are welcome to bring a wood blank of their own (we recommend Rockler if purchasing in advance). Join us for a night of woodturning community, guidance, and fun! Thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop and Matt Iannacci for his expertise and enthusiasm! Tuition: $45 Materials: The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, or students can BYOB (blank)! Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist: Matt Iannacci “I have been woodturning for over 10 years, and doing wood flatwork for more than 7 years. I focus on medium-sized peices (vases, urns, etc., in woodturning, and jewelry boxes and frames in flatwork), usually seeking to combine different wood species to provide color and texture in my pieces. I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: Lily Vakili & her band at The Govt Center!
events.description: Catch Lily Vakili on her Live Wire tour, with special guests Philly-based roots rockers Mighty Joe Castro & the Gravamen! “…compelling the way the first Patti Smith music gripped a listener, The Swans’ Jarboe enthralled or even Nico startled” – Americana Highways “The audience was in her palm. Not one phone was raised, not one distracted look… This felt intimate, this felt personal, this felt like what live music used to be when musicians and audience shared something real..” – New England SoundsAbout Lily's latest project - the EP LIVE WIRE, Americana Highways says: “…‘Anybody Knows,’ a crawling, dirty blues song that underlines Vakili’s smoldering, femme fatale vocals…‘Heart’s Afire’ drifts and oozes on Hart’s fat, round bassline as Vakili’s drawling, breathy vocals imbue the lyrics with simmering passion…this track summons suggestions of Springsteen’s ‘I’m On Fire.’ Both are enormously sensual and unapologetic. Tangs of swampy blues textures give ‘I’ve Been Hiding’ an ooey gooey flow, while at the same time providing a nasty, bluesy matrix for Vakili’s deliciously howling voice”. Born in Honduras to a family of six, Lily Vakili was raised across Honduras, Florida, Thailand, Puerto Rico, and Iowa absorbing pieces of each place, each culture, along the way. This shaped her voice, her worldview, and her lifelong search for connection. Before she found her footing in music, Vakili built a life as a dancer, an actor, a lawyer, and a mother. She was drawn to songwriting not by ambition or industry, but by a deep, undeniable need to give voice to the world around her. The past decade has seen her channel that force through 6 studio albums released both as a solo artist and with Vakili Band each one experimenting with the wide, untamed possibilities of rock. "I love the serendipitous nature of art, Vakili says. It’s disruptive, it’s intentional, it’s an exertion of will."About Mighty Joe Castro & The Gravamen:“..a noir-tinged journey through vintage rock ‘n’ roll, americana, and gothic storytelling. It’s a reverb-drenched landscape, full of vibrant tunes and arresting lyrics. “ – Americana UK“Mighty Joe Castro and the Gravamen don’t make music for those that are trying to relive the Golden Age of Rock’ n’ Roll. They’re writing soulful songs for the people who are giving everything that they have to the struggle of living through these times. These are the kinds of songs that Buddy Holly or Johnny Cash might feel obliged to write as a way to answer our collective anxieties. ” – Alt77.comMighty Joe Castro & The Gravamen hail from Philadelphia, PA, blending the vintage swagger of 1950s rock ‘n’ roll with a gritty, modern edge. Imagine Buddy Holly armed with a stack of effect pedals and some of Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds records. That’s the vibe.Their sound is rooted in classic rockabilly, but it’s filtered through a postmodern lens—complete with sonic Easter eggs cribbed from old episodes of MTV’s 120 Minutes. Frontman Mighty Joe Castro crafts sharp, lyric-driven songs, while The Gravamen build cinematic atmospheres with Link Wray-meets-Jesus and Mary Chain guitars, booming doghouse bass, and foot-stomping swing beats. The band occupies a unique crossroads where Sun Records and Creation Records collide.

events.title: The Format w/ Get Up Kids
events.description: The Format with The Get Up Kids brings together two beloved bands known for emotionally driven songwriting and influential contributions to indie rock and emo music. The Format, led by Nate Ruess and Sam Means, became known for blending indie pop, piano-driven melodies, and heartfelt lyrics into energetic and theatrical alternative rock songs. Their music balances catchy hooks with introspective storytelling, creating a sound that remains influential among indie and pop-rock fans.The Get Up Kids helped shape the late 1990s and early 2000s emo and alternative rock scene through emotionally charged lyrics, melodic guitar work, and energetic punk-inspired performances. Their music combines heartfelt vulnerability with upbeat instrumentation, making them one of the defining bands of the emo revival era. Together, the lineup creates a nostalgic and emotionally resonant concert experience filled with passionate performances, singalong choruses, and influential alternative rock sounds.

The group has earned acclaim for heartfelt songwriting, rich harmonies, and a sound that pays tribute to classic country traditions while maintaining a contemporary edge. Their music often explores themes of hard work, love, resilience, small-town life, and the experiences of everyday people through vivid storytelling and memorable melodies. Known for energetic live performances and a deep connection to country music's roots, Silverada continues to carry forward the spirit of classic Texas country for a new generation of fans.

events.title: The Serpent's Skin
events.description:
We are excited to bring you a screening of The Serpent's Skin (2025), Directed by Alice Maio Mackay (T Blockers, Carnage for Christmas, Our Effed Up World).

Twentysomething Anna (Alexandra McVicker, October Crow) finally leaves her small, transmisogynistic hometown for good and quickly begins dating goth tattoo artist Gen (Avalon Fast, Castration Movie) after the two discover they share supernatural powers.

But before Anna can call up the U-Haul, Gen inadvertently summons a demon through the sick neck tattoo she gives sensitive guitarist Danny (Jordan Dulieu). As Danny — or whatever’s inside of him — begins feeding off their friends, it’s up to Anna and Gen to figure out how to use their powers to save everyone before it’s too late.

Running at 83 minutes, the movie channels the visual language of 90s teenage horror like Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Charmed while inserting the disillusionment and hallucinogenic surrealism of Gregg Araki's Teen Apocalypse Trilogy - making for a refreshing, titillating trans lesbian story.

Doors open at 7 :30 PM with the screening to start at 8 PM. Snacks and drinks provided. Please mask when not eating or drinking, and stay home if you're sick. Limited pay-what-you-can tickets at the door.

events.title: JAY JURDEN
events.description: Jay Jurden Jay Jurden is the star of the new Hulu comedy special Yes Ma’am, a breakout hour that solidifies him as one of the sharpest and most original comedic voices working today. Based in New York and originally from Mississippi, Jay has become a national standout thanks to his precise writing, magnetic presence, and a point of view that is both deeply personal and universally funny. The special is now available on all streaming platforms. Why'd We Book It? Watching Jay and Caleb on the So True podcast last year brought us to tears. Jay has such a distict voice as a writer and you can feel his energy through the writing on The Problem with Jon Stewart. Jay is extremely charasmatic and his shows are full of nonstop laughs. His wit when talking about his experience growing up Southern, Black, and queer is personal and genuine. We are excited to have him at Bottlerocket soon! For Fans Of... Gianmarco Soresi, Dylan Adler, Caleb Hearon Extended Bio: Jay is a four-time guest on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon and has also appeared on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, The Late Late Show with James Corden, Comedy Central Featuring, and HBO’s High Maintenance. He was a Staff Writer for Apple TV+’s Emmy-nominated The Problem with Jon Stewart, bringing his distinctive comedic insight to one of television’s most influential political-comedy series. In 2022, Jay was named one of Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch, and his debut comedy album Jay Jurden Y’all premiered at #1 on iTunes. His writing has appeared in The New Yorker, Vulture, Teen Vogue, McSweeney’s, and Marvel’s Voices: X-Men #1, showcasing a range that extends well beyond stand-up. Jay was also featured on Vulture’s Comedians You Should and Will Know list and selected for the prestigious Just For Laughs: New Faces. Jay tours nationwide, selling out clubs and theaters with an electric, high-precision act that continues to resonate across audiences. Seating/Show Information: This show will have theater seating. events.title: The Unsolved Mystery of Ms Patsy Climbe
events.description:
Guess who is hitting the road?? The Nocturnal Creatures Troupe is going on tour, and you just might catch us creepin’ in a city near you!

Nocturnal Creatures Troupe presents: The Unsolved Mystery of Ms. Patsy Climb
An absurd puppet musical exploring the lives of three misfits on their quest to make it as street performers in the French Quarter of New Orleans. The Trio gets into all sorts of shenanigans, from getting addicted to “Crusties Hotdog Stand” , to refuting allegations of eating an ex lovers head. The story is narrated by Detective Bark, who uses his keen senses and logical mind to sniff out clues from the baffling events that have occurred. Will the creatures find fame? Or will struggles between the bandmates stop them from getting picked up by a label? Is their lead glockenspiel a blood thirsty diva? Will Detective Bark be able to crack this case wide open, and earn the title “GOOD BOY”? All these questions answered and more in The Nocturnal Creatures Show!!

We are so excited to be joined by our magical friend and skilled puppeteer Maya, @teethforbangs !!! YAY

events.description: Dennett is an American electronic music producer and DJ known for combining soaring melodic textures with powerful bass-driven drops to create an energetic yet emotionally resonant sound. Originally discovering music production while living in Southern California before continuing his career in Arizona, he has steadily built a reputation within the bass music community for pushing creative boundaries and experimenting with new production techniques. His releases blend elements of melodic bass, dubstep, future bass, and house, balancing cinematic atmospheres with festival-ready intensity that appeals to a wide range of electronic music fans. Dennett has performed at major festivals and clubs across the United States, earning recognition for dynamic live sets that showcase both technical precision and an adventurous musical style. As his catalog and audience continue to grow, Dennett has established himself as one of the emerging talents in electronic dance music, driven by a commitment to innovation and an unmistakable passion for creating immersive sonic experiences.

events.title: Fort Ligonier Days
events.description: See the site that changed world history and inspired Fort Ligonier Days! The historic site comes to life with battle demonstrations, cannon firings, encampments and more to commemorate the historic October 12, 1758, attack on Fort Ligonier. Stop by Sutlers Row located on the front lawn of the museum and see 18th-century-inspired artisans, and Mount Vernon's Resident Baker Justin Cherry and his Half Crown Bakehouse.Schedule of artillery firings and historical demonstrations to be announced soon!Sutlers RowAn 18th century artisan marketplace located on the Museum’s front lawn featuring Justin Cherry, Mount Vernon’s Baker in Residence, and his Half Crown Bakehouse. Justin rises in the middle of the night to fire up his massive clay beehive oven to bake batches of multi-grain bread made with heirloom grains and served warm with salt pork butter, inspired by 18th century soldiers’ rations. Try to stop early! Justin sells out each year!Living HistoryVisitors are encouraged to engage with reenactors and ask questions about clothing, living conditions, their military history and more.World-Class MuseumDiscover the important archaeological finds and how they informed the reconstruction of the fort to within mere inches of where it originally stood and how throughout the decades of Fort Ligonier Days, the reenactment of the October 12, 1758, Battle of Fort Ligonier has remained a central event during the festivities.Not to miss is the museum’s new America 250 exhibit “To Rise and Fight Again: The Road to Revolution Begins at Fort Ligonier.”Regular admission applies except for youth ages 17 and under who are free Saturday and Sunday thanks to the generous sponsorship of Fort Ligonier Days, Inc.Visitor parking is not available at Fort Ligonier during Fort Ligonier Days weekend. Parking is available at designated festival lots with shuttle bus services provided.

events.title: New & Noted: Ayad Akhtar
events.description: A mysterious accident along a country road sparks an awakening and an investigation in Pulitzer Prize–winning playwright and acclaimed novelist Ayad Akhtar’s most daring work yet—a visionary novel of spiritual transformation in an age of fracture—“bordering at times on the ineffable” (Mary Gaitskill).When a hit-and-run shatters more than his body, a writer is caught between revelation and madness as an uncanny pull toward a brilliant campus colleague ensnares him in a scandal that threatens to destroy them both. What begins as a provocative portrait of academic and cultural warfare deepens into erotic entanglement, the exposure of a family secret, and the mystery surrounding the narrator’s accident—both the violence and its aftermath.Moving between rural America and Europe, Islam and Christianity, the intimate and the metaphysical, The Radiance is of our American moment and beyond it—asking not only what has broken, but what radiance remains.Ayad Akhtar is a novelist and playwright. His work has been published and performed in over two dozen languages. He is the winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the Edith Wharton Citation of Merit for Fiction, and an award in literature from the American Academy of Arts and Letters, among other honors. Akhtar is the author of the novels American Dervish, a Kirkus Reviews Best Book of the Year, and Homeland Elegies, named one of 10 Best Books of 2020 by The New York Times. He has also authored the plays McNeal, Junk, Disgraced, The Who & The What, and The Invisible Hand. Akhtar was named the New York State Author in 2021.

events.title: Teddy Duchamp's Army Record Release Show
events.description:
Teddy DuChamp's Army have a new record in 2026!
"...the spirit never dies."
is being released on October 9th via legendary Philly punk label Creep Records and Sweet Cheetah in the US, Engineer Records in the UK and Scene police Records in Europe.

This records features J Robbins (JAWBOX, Burning Airlines, Government Issue) on bass.
Mario Quintero (Spotlights, Shiner, Molly Mcguire, Sisters) on 2nd guitar as well as the return of Mike Rock on guitar, Andy Wright on vox, and Jeff Kopanic on drums.
The album was produced and engineered by J Robbins at his Magpie Cage studio in Baltimore in January 2026 and mixed and mastered by Mario Quintero.
11 brand new songs! Punchy, melodic, with heavy, mellow and fast moments spread throughout classic TDA with a fresher feel.

Joining them will be Trace Remains - (ex Pikadori/Allies) Joey and Joel still being one of the best guitar duo's in Pittsburgh.

Latecomer - good old fast melodic punk in the vein of your favorite Lookout Records stuff

One If By Land - Fred and the boys have been doing it for years up in meadville/Franklin area with the Twirpentines and Signal Home. OIBL might be their best project to date, if you haven't seen them yet, get on it!

Show is Friday Oct.9th 6:30 doors at TECH 25 in Mt. Oliver only 2 blocks from 222 Ormsby and a short distance from Bottle Rocket. just two blocks off Brownsville road and on the busline.
112 St. Joseph St. Mt . Oliver 15210
ALL AGES and Alcohol with ID over 21 w/ donation. Beer donated by The Smiling Moose Brewery

There are multiple parking lots available around the building and street parking.

For those unfamiliar TECH 25 (run by Pete Spynda of Pandemic and Pittonkatonk) is an awesome noprofit that teaches classes on recording , live sound, lighting, rigging and many aspects of recording and live event production. We are stoked to help them shed some light on the space and their mission.
The Shiner show happened there last year and was awesome, we can't wait to have the show in this space.

events.title: The Yeoman of the Guard
events.description:
The Yeomen of the Guard; or, The Merryman and His Maid is set within the Tower of London during the 16th century, where love, loyalty, and deception intertwine beneath the shadow of the executioner’s axe. Colonel Fairfax, a nobleman unjustly condemned to die, devises an unexpected plan to preserve his inheritance, drawing the spirited strolling singer Elsie Maynard and the Tower’s colorful inhabitants into a web of disguises, mistaken identities, and romantic entanglements. As comedy gives way to moments of genuine tenderness and heartbreak, The Yeomen of the Guard explores themes of honor, sacrifice, and the unpredictable nature of love in one of Gilbert & Sullivan’s most emotionally resonant works.

The Yeomen of the Guard is Gilbert & Sullivan’s eleventh collaboration, and premiered in October 1888 at the Savoy Theatre in London. While it retains the wit and memorable melodies for which the pair are celebrated, the opera is distinguished by its richer emotional depth and more serious dramatic tone, making it one of the most unique operettas in the canon.

@carre__carre

Carré is one of the leading figureheads in an international cohort of female, queer and non-binary producers pushing deep dubstep - alongside Too Far Gone favorites EMA, Darwin, Introspekt, Beatrice M and the Queer Steppa don, CCL - representing a refreshing shift in a genre that has long been heavily male-dominated, opening up a more inclusive space while also pushing a sound whose deep and meditative qualities speak to the dub part of dubstep.

UK dubstep’s lineage is the backbone of Carré’s sound where she balances a fine mix of sensual low-end rollers, percussive left-field techno, chrome-plated dubstep, and wonky drum workouts.

She has graced imprints like SPE:C, Bait, Woozy, and the formative dubstep imprint, Tempa ( @tempa.ltd ). Her latest string of EPs, Hibiscus + Citrine, highlight spacious rollers with US rap-meets-dubstep crossover - making it clear that she’s thoroughly comfortable weaving her own stew of influences into the modern bass music recipe.
With the dubstep baton finally passing to a new guard, Carré has cemented her role as one of its torchbearers.

@formosa.exe

Outside from being one half of the city’s most in-demand party collective, Steph is a champion of the PGH dance underground - always willing to dot-connect, share knowledge or nerd out on her impeccable/extensive musical taste. Very lucky to have Formosa join us for opening duties where she will take us into the breakbeat-heavy depths of her sonic palette.

events.title: A Conversation with the Artist: Melissa English Campbell
events.description: Join us for a conversation with artist Melissa English Campbell as she shares her concept behind the works featured in Bodies in Motion. Join us for an engaging conversation with artist Melissa English Campbell as she shares the story, ideas, materials and processes behind her work. Through an informal interview and audience Q&A, gain deeper insight into the exhibition! Bodies in Motion (Currently on view through 10/31/2026) Bodies in Motion balances the strangeness of shifting realities with the familiarity and comfort of textiles. It is a partially immersive installation evoking proximity to textiles such as a warm towel or playing near blankets and sheets on a clothesline. The exhibition emerged when artist Melissa English Campbell recognized her tendency to mirror others’ accents, tone, and mannerisms as an unconscious survival strategy; a frequent adaptive response often shared by immigrants and their daughters. This experience is expressed through warp painted weavings presented in mirrored pairs. While images repeat, each work retains its own character, creating larger compositions that hold similarity and difference in productive tension. Panels are suspended throughout the gallery and on the walls, the textiles absorb sound and sway gently with air currents and passing bodies. Water recurs as a central motif, reflecting the fluid nature of identity and the body’s search for both challenge and comfort, as well as sanctuary from social expectations. Through repetition, comfort and strangeness, mirroring, and movement, Bodies in Motion invites viewers to consider identity not as fixed, but as something continuously shaped by adaptation, belonging, and change. Melissa English Campbell (b. 1969, San Francisco) holds a B.S. in Environmental Design from the University of California, Davis, and an MFA in Studio Arts from Kent State University. Her artwork has been exhibited globally, including at the Royal Albert Museum in the UK, Seoul, South Korea; Como, Italy; and New South Wales, Australia. Nationally, Melissa’s work has been shown at galleries such as San Jose Museum of Textiles, Columbus Museum of Craft, New Bedford Art Museum, Museum of Texas Tech University; Petaluma Center for the Arts, Hand Weaving Museum, and Contemporary Craft. She is a recipient of the Award of Excellence from the Ohio Council for the Arts. Recent artist residencies include The Chautauqua Institutes Artist Residency, Vermont Studio Center, Praxis TC2 Residency, and Berea College Artist Residency. Campbell currently lives and works in Northeast Ohio. Photo: Feet in Fawn Lake (detail), Courtesy of the Artist

events.title: RAD Pass: Hand Papermaking with Collage and Inclusions with Katy Dement
events.description: This class will focus on collage composition, and "wet on wet" techniques unique to hand papermaking. RAD Pass Workshop Please note: This workshop is being offered exclusively through RAD Pass . To read more about RAD Pass and to register for this workshop, please click on the link above. The program is open to any Allegheny County resident with a library card. 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 10 Time: 2:00-5:00pm Description: This class will focus on rules of collage composition, and “wet on wet” techniques unique to hand papermaking. We will be illustrating with natural and found materials, as well as vintage ephemera while covering archival collage making and adhesives and becoming familiar with the Holland beater and a variety of tools. Many wet paper sheets will be crafted and embellished with random inclusions and seeds as we hone our sheet forming skills and discover the properties and limitations of handmade papers. We will cover the history of paper making and discuss intended uses of handmade paper. Participants are encouraged to bring memorabilia from home to add to the narrative. Tuition: All tuition and materials are complimentary thanks to RAD Pass! Materials: All materials will be provided but students are encouraged to bring any natural, fibrous materials, dried and pressed plants and other personal memorabilia from home. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Papers Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to attend One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hallway from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call (and leave a message for) Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist For my entire life I have been a working artist, organic gardener, and beekeeper. I create handmade paper as a means to an end. Paper art works take the form of: art lighting, shadow box, stationary, books and sculptures all crafted from sustainably collected plants, recycled and invasive fibers. Each piece is a vignette that holds a visual narrative. Through layers of vintage ephemera, photos and bits of cloth, tales are told. When etched images are included the dialogue begins. Toys, natural and found objects punctuate the story. No material is arbitrary; I am influenced by overlooked materials found in my community, my own back yard. Rusty old tools are mashed together with deconstructed plants; this is where I find humor, combining these unlikely fellows. Often my works invite the viewer to playfully interact with the art work through light and kinetic elements that bring the imagery to life.

events.title: Historic Graveyard Tours at Trinity Cathedral | Downtown Pittsburgh
events.description: Explore centuries of Pittsburgh history during a guided tour of the historic graveyard at Trinity Episcopal Cathedral in Downtown Pittsburgh.Long before Pittsburgh became a city, and before the United States became a country, people were being buried on the land where Trinity Cathedral stands today. This October, visitors can explore this remarkable burial ground and discover the people, stories, and surprising details preserved there.Trinity’s Historic Graveyard Tours take guests through one of Downtown Pittsburgh’s oldest burial grounds, sharing stories that connect the site to the early history and development of Pittsburgh. Guests will explore the graveyard, search for historic details hidden among the markers, and step inside Trinity Cathedral as part of the experience.Tours are offered Saturday, October 10, and Saturday, October 24, with multiple afternoon tour times and a special Dusk Tour as daylight fades.Dates & TimesSaturday, October 103:00 PM4:30 PM6:00 PM Dusk TourSaturday, October 242:30 PM4:00 PM5:30 PM Dusk TourAdmission: $15 afternoon tours | $20 Dusk ToursLocation: Trinity Episcopal Cathedral, 328 Sixth Avenue, Downtown Pittsburgh, PA 15222Capacity: Limited to 20 guests per tourThese guided historic tours offer a distinctive way to experience Pittsburgh history during the Halloween season and are ideal for history lovers, architecture and historic-site enthusiasts, curious Pittsburghers, and visitors looking for unique things to do in Pittsburgh this October.Advance tickets are recommended due to limited tour capacity.

events.title: Martin Sexton
events.description: Martin Sexton is an acclaimed singer-songwriter whose performances blend rock, folk, soul, gospel, blues and R&B. Known for his remarkable vocal range, expressive fingerpicking and engaging stage presence, he creates concerts that can move effortlessly from upbeat boogie-woogie and blues to intimate ballads. Sexton’s catalog includes seven studio albums, four live releases and two EPs, with songs shaped by his early years as a street performer and his gift for connecting directly with audiences. His music offers a soulful, genre-spanning experience for listeners who value exceptional musicianship and heartfelt songwriting.

events.title: Pittsburgh Opera: Rigoletto
events.description: RIGOLETTOMusic by Giuseppe VerdiLibretto by Francesco Maria PiaveBased on the play Le Roi s’Amuse by Victor Hugo • OCTOBER 10, 16, 18, 2026A fool’s errand.Sharp-witted court jester Rigoletto is the philandering Duke’s right-hand man, always quick to defend his patron’s womanizing and mock his master’s victims. But the joke is on him.The tables turn when Rigoletto and the Duke are both cursed for their wretched behavior. While Rigoletto instinctively fears the curse, the callous Duke remains unfazed, turning his rakish intentions toward Rigoletto’s daughter, Gilda.Naïve, sheltered, and easily charmed, Gilda falls madly in love with the Duke. Now, Rigoletto must plot and scheme to save his own daughter from the monster he had championed. Will Rigoletto have the last laugh, or will he be the punchline?

This year, Old Economy Village is partnering with Beaver County Paranormal, whose years of knowledge and experience make this the perfect chance to learn the ins and outs of paranormal investigating and get professional input on your experiences. We encourage you to bring any small handheld ghost-hunting equipment and your sense of adventure. There are no costumed figures or scares. This is a chance to explore the Village after dark and draw your own conclusions.

events.title: Modest Mouse with Caroline Rose
events.description: Modest Mouse with Caroline Rose brings together two inventive indie artists known for unconventional songwriting, energetic performances, and genre-blending creativity. Modest Mouse became one of the defining indie rock bands of the 2000s through angular guitar work, introspective lyrics, and a sound that combines alternative rock, post-punk, and experimental influences. Their music often explores themes of existentialism, isolation, modern life, and emotional unpredictability through distinctive vocals and dynamic instrumentation.Caroline Rose adds a bold and eclectic indie-pop presence fueled by witty songwriting, theatrical performances, and a fearless approach to genre experimentation. Their music blends synth-pop, rock, electronic textures, and satirical storytelling into colorful and highly engaging live shows. Together, the lineup creates a vibrant concert experience filled with artistic unpredictability, emotional depth, and inventive alternative music.

events.title: Calliope Presents Rachel Sumner & Traveling Light
events.description: Rachel Sumner & Traveling Light are a Boston-based string band making music that blends folk tradition with feminist storytelling, poetic detail, and just enough grit. At the center is Sumner’s songwriting—rooted in history, myth, and personal reckoning—carried by close harmonies, upright bass, acoustic guitar, and fiddle. The trio features Kat Wallace on fiddle and vocals and Mike Siegel on upright bass and vocals, whose playing brings both tension and tenderness to the sound.Their sound is spare and intimate, sometimes eerie, sometimes sweet, always intentional. They call it Femericana—sharp-edged Americana with a splash of feminine rage.Sumner has performed at the Library of Congress, where five of her original songs are now archived, and was a 2024 winner of the Kerrville New Folk competition. Her song “Radium Girls (Curie Eleison)” struck a nerve—streamed over 300,000 times and picked up by dancers, theater directors, and deep listeners who saw themselves in its story. It’s been tattooed on arms, sung in audition rooms, and carried into classrooms and protests. The kind of song people hold onto.

events.title: The Yeoman of the Guard
events.description:
The Yeomen of the Guard; or, The Merryman and His Maid is set within the Tower of London during the 16th century, where love, loyalty, and deception intertwine beneath the shadow of the executioner’s axe. Colonel Fairfax, a nobleman unjustly condemned to die, devises an unexpected plan to preserve his inheritance, drawing the spirited strolling singer Elsie Maynard and the Tower’s colorful inhabitants into a web of disguises, mistaken identities, and romantic entanglements. As comedy gives way to moments of genuine tenderness and heartbreak, The Yeomen of the Guard explores themes of honor, sacrifice, and the unpredictable nature of love in one of Gilbert & Sullivan’s most emotionally resonant works.

The Yeomen of the Guard is Gilbert & Sullivan’s eleventh collaboration, and premiered in October 1888 at the Savoy Theatre in London. While it retains the wit and memorable melodies for which the pair are celebrated, the opera is distinguished by its richer emotional depth and more serious dramatic tone, making it one of the most unique operettas in the canon.

events.title: Book Talk and Signing with Americana Corner’s Tom Hand
events.description: Join us during Fort Ligonier Days weekend for a special America 250 event featuring a Talk and Book Signing of "America Victorius" by Mr. Tom Hand.Mr. Hand is the founder and publisher of Americana Corner; a platform he launched in 2020 to share and preserve the story of America’s founding era. Through weekly articles and videos, he brings to life the pivotal events, foundational documents, and figures who shaped the United States, aiming to rekindle a spirit of patriotism and historical appreciation in his fellow citizens.Mr. Hand’s passion for telling the Great American Story extends to preserving its cultural and historical treasures through the Preserving America program, funded through his Americana Corner Foundation. This nationwide initiative supports a diverse range of projects through grants, fosters long-term partnerships with historical organizations, and annually hosts the Preserving America Conference that brings together leaders in preservation and public history to share best practices, exchange ideas, and inspire collaboration.Mr. Hand’s Preserving America program generously supports Fort Ligonier’s History Alive! program, an engaging experience for visitors to learn about the daily life of a frontier military outpost in North America during the 18th century. Weekends feature 18 century-inspired artisans, tradesmen, musicians, historical military units, and more who depict the culture and lifestyle of the colonial era.Copies of America Victorious Lesser-Known Campaigns and Commanders that Helped Win American Independence –– a companion volume that highlights the lesser-known heroes who fought for our nation’s independence across countless battlefields in the early republic are available for purchase at Fort Ligonier’s Museum Store.The book talk begins at 11:00 AM followed by the signing. Regular admission applies.

events.title: The Yeoman of the Guard
events.description:
The Yeomen of the Guard; or, The Merryman and His Maid is set within the Tower of London during the 16th century, where love, loyalty, and deception intertwine beneath the shadow of the executioner’s axe. Colonel Fairfax, a nobleman unjustly condemned to die, devises an unexpected plan to preserve his inheritance, drawing the spirited strolling singer Elsie Maynard and the Tower’s colorful inhabitants into a web of disguises, mistaken identities, and romantic entanglements. As comedy gives way to moments of genuine tenderness and heartbreak, The Yeomen of the Guard explores themes of honor, sacrifice, and the unpredictable nature of love in one of Gilbert & Sullivan’s most emotionally resonant works.

The Yeomen of the Guard is Gilbert & Sullivan’s eleventh collaboration, and premiered in October 1888 at the Savoy Theatre in London. While it retains the wit and memorable melodies for which the pair are celebrated, the opera is distinguished by its richer emotional depth and more serious dramatic tone, making it one of the most unique operettas in the canon.

events.description: Stephen Day is a Nashville-based singer-songwriter whose music blends soulful pop, folk, and Americana influences with thoughtful storytelling and an inviting vocal style. Raised in Georgia, he developed a passion for songwriting at an early age and has since built a reputation for crafting songs that balance emotional depth with memorable melodies. His work often explores themes of love, personal growth, nostalgia, and human connection, delivered through lyrics that feel both introspective and universally relatable. Day's recordings showcase a warm, organic sound that draws inspiration from classic singer-songwriters while embracing modern production techniques, allowing his music to appeal to a wide audience. Through extensive touring, a growing catalog of acclaimed releases, and a strong connection with listeners, Stephen Day continues to establish himself as one of the most promising emerging voices in the contemporary singer-songwriter landscape.

events.title: Penn And Teller
events.description: Penn & Teller are the legendary illusionists, comedians, and entertainers who have redefined the art of magic through their unique blend of astonishing illusions, sharp wit, and theatrical storytelling. Performing together for decades, the duo has become internationally renowned for combining world-class sleight of hand, large-scale illusions, and thought-provoking demonstrations with Penn Jillette's energetic narration and Teller's signature silent performance style. Their acclaimed stage productions challenge audiences' expectations by revealing selected techniques while simultaneously creating even more astonishing mysteries, proving that the artistry of illusion extends far beyond simply keeping secrets. In addition to their long-running Las Vegas residency and hit television series Penn & Teller: Fool Us, they have authored books, appeared in films and television, and inspired generations of magicians through their creativity and innovation. Whether performing intimate close-up magic or breathtaking grand illusions, Penn & Teller deliver an unforgettable live experience that seamlessly blends comedy, intelligence, audience participation, and seemingly impossible feats.

During Sensory Friendly time, you can see and touch biofacts, including eggs and feathers, and enjoy a sensory-friendly version of Passport to Parks, presented by AAA Travel at 11 am. Plus, visit our sensory table and explore our Interactive Play Spaces, including a larger-than-life Draw Alive station. Sensory Bags from KultureCity, featuring items like headphones and fidget toys, are available to borrow daily at the National Aviary.A helpful sensory guide to the sights, sounds, and climate of the Aviary's habitats can be viewed in advance AND during your trip. Please register in advance!

Enjoy a casual stroll through history and horticulture during this .5-mile walk.Explore the the natural world with the Frick's ongoing Living Collection Series. Through walks, tours, lectures, and more, the Living Collection Series uses the Frick's grounds as the backdrop for learning and connection. As an accredited arboretum, the site features dozens of varieties of trees and shrubs, in addition to decorative and vegetable gardens and a historic greenhouse.

events.title: Christone Kingfish Ingram
events.description: Christone “Kingfish” Ingram is a powerhouse blues guitarist, singer and songwriter from Clarksdale, Mississippi, celebrated for bringing Delta tradition into conversation with rock, soul, funk, hip-hop and jazz. His electrifying performances pair fiery guitar work with deeply personal storytelling, making him one of contemporary blues’ most compelling live artists. Ingram’s Grammy-winning album 662 and acclaimed live release Live in London helped establish his international reputation, while his latest project, Hard Road, explores love, loss, identity and perseverance through a harder-edged blend of blues, rock and R&B. The result is a vibrant, modern sound rooted in the genre’s enduring legacy.

events.title: Tab Benoit (21+ Event)
events.description: Tab Benoit is a Louisiana singer, guitarist and songwriter known for swamp blues shaped by Cajun, roots-rock and soul influences. He emerged nationally with his 1992 debut, Nice and Warm, and has continued developing a distinctly Southern sound across albums including Wetlands, a blues meditation on Louisiana’s threatened environment, and Medicine, which won three Blues Music Awards. Benoit also co-founded Voice of the Wetlands, an environmental music project focused on preserving south Louisiana’s coastal wetlands. His gritty vocals, electric-guitar work and deep connection to Louisiana’s musical traditions define his catalog.

events.title: Light & Unite for Pregnancy & Infant Loss Awareness Day
events.description: Light & Unite is Pittsburgh Bereavement Doulas’ annual remembrance gathering for families who have experienced pregnancy or infant loss. Each year we come together with bereaved parents, loved ones, and community members to honor the babies who are deeply loved and always remembered.Our gathering takes place on Pregnancy & Infant Loss Awareness Day, October 15, when communities around the world participate in the International Wave of Light—a candle-lighting ceremony that moves across time zones in quiet solidarity. Families light candles, share space with others who understand loss, and take a moment to remember their babies together.Join us at Schenley Plaza for a gentle, family-friendly evening of community, memorial art, music, light, and Pittsburgh’s 7:00 p.m. Wave of Light. Guests are invited to wear white.Light & Unite offers a gentle space to pause, remember, and gather with others who understand. events.title: A Celebration of International Poetry
events.description: Born in 1978 in Santo Domingo, Frank Báez has made a name for himself as one of the Dominican Republic’s most relevant poets and nonfiction writers. He has published six poetry books, a short story collection, and four nonfiction books. He is a founding member of El Hombrecito, the first Dominican Spoken Word band, which has three albums to its credit. His work has appeared in numerous anthologies, and translations of his books of poetry have been published in Arabic, Dutch, German, and Bangla. Two of his books have been translated into English: Last Night I Dreamt I Was a DJ (2014) and The End of the World Came to My Neighborhood (2022).P. Scott Cunningham is the author of Self-Portrait as the “i” in Florida (Autumn House, 2026), winner of the 2025 Donald Justice Poetry Prize, and Ya Te Veo (University of Arkansas, 2018), selected for the Miller Williams Poetry Series and a finalist for the National Poetry Series. His poems, essays, and translations have appeared in The Nation, American Poetry Review, Gulf Coast, POETRY, A Public Space, Harvard Review, Michigan Quarterly Review, Monocle, and The Guardian, among others. Born and raised in South Florida, he lives with his family in Illinois.Sony Ton-Aime is the Executive Director of Pittsburgh Arts & Lectures and the author of Konbit (Carnegie Mellon University Press, 2026).

events.title: The Brook and The Bluff
events.description: The Brook & The Bluff is an indie-pop quartet celebrated for its lush vocal harmonies, sophisticated songwriting, and easygoing blend of folk, soul, and alternative influences. Originally formed by longtime friends from Alabama before relocating to Nashville, the band has built a loyal following through its warm, organic sound and emotionally expressive performances. Their music combines intricate guitar work, smooth rhythmic grooves, and layered harmonies to create songs that explore themes of love, change, self-discovery, and human connection with both honesty and optimism. Releases such as First Place, Yard Sale, and a growing collection of acclaimed singles have showcased the group's ability to craft memorable melodies while continually refining its distinctive musical identity. Known for intimate yet energetic live shows and exceptional vocal chemistry, The Brook & The Bluff continues to establish itself as one of the most compelling emerging acts in today's indie music scene.

events.title: Destination Deco: Steel City Deco
events.description: Experience the magic of Art Deco in Pittsburgh!Join the Art Deco Society of New York this October for a private, Art Deco-filled immersive weekend in one of the best-preserved concentrations of Art Deco commercial towers outside New York and Chicago: Pittsburgh.Discover with us the region that inspired Frank Lloyd Wright's signature masterpiece Fallingwater and see it in all its blazing autumn glory on our day-long exploration of Wright's celebrated icons.On our three-day weekend, we will explore the best of Pittsburgh's Art Deco through a VIP tour built around the extraordinary architecture and design of the 1920s and 1930s, when the money flowed and Pittsburgh steel built the era's most enduring icons across America.A highlight of the weekend is a private curated visit to the Carnegie Museum of Art for an up-close look at The Chariot of Aurora, the monumental Dupas and Dunand panel that once graced the Grand Salon of SS Normandie. We will not only hear about its restoration over two years, but also stories about other treasures from the museum’s Art Deco collection.On this in-depth adventure designed especially for lovers of Art Deco, you'll explore, tour, and dine with fellow Deco enthusiasts as we immerse ourselves in the interwar architecture that makes Pittsburgh one of America's best-kept architectural secrets. We'll see soaring skyscrapers, stunning halls of learning, and grand government buildings through a mix of special access and private tours. On the final day of our memorable weekend, we have been invited for a private tour of an Art Moderne home designed to resemble the bridge of an Art Deco ocean liner. Throughout the trip, we'll hear the stories of the industrialists and the artists and city shapers they commissioned to build their headquarters in what was the crown jewel of American heavy industry.Space is extremely limited. Early registration is strongly encouraged.

events.title: The Yeoman of the Guard
events.description:
The Yeomen of the Guard; or, The Merryman and His Maid is set within the Tower of London during the 16th century, where love, loyalty, and deception intertwine beneath the shadow of the executioner’s axe. Colonel Fairfax, a nobleman unjustly condemned to die, devises an unexpected plan to preserve his inheritance, drawing the spirited strolling singer Elsie Maynard and the Tower’s colorful inhabitants into a web of disguises, mistaken identities, and romantic entanglements. As comedy gives way to moments of genuine tenderness and heartbreak, The Yeomen of the Guard explores themes of honor, sacrifice, and the unpredictable nature of love in one of Gilbert & Sullivan’s most emotionally resonant works.

The Yeomen of the Guard is Gilbert & Sullivan’s eleventh collaboration, and premiered in October 1888 at the Savoy Theatre in London. While it retains the wit and memorable melodies for which the pair are celebrated, the opera is distinguished by its richer emotional depth and more serious dramatic tone, making it one of the most unique operettas in the canon.

events.title: History Alive! Geo. Franks, Hatter, Authentically Recreated Historical Hats
events.description: Watch George Franks handcraft a historical hat from the colonial-era 1701-1799!Geo. Franks, Hatter offers hand crafted, round blocked historical hats in wool felt and fur. All patterns are documented. All methods and materials are correct to the period and sewn by hand by the hatter himself.George’s hats are featured in museum exhibits, worn at historic sites, in personal collections, and worn by discriminating living historians. He is a former officer and Governor of the Company of Military historians and remains active in the Brigade of the American Revolution and Continental Line.History Alive! at Fort Ligonier is an engaging experience for visitors to learn more about the daily life of a frontier military outpost in North America during the 18th century. Through daily programming depicting typical activities of a military site such as soldiering, manual labor, tailoring, laundry, and cooking, and special weekend demonstrations from 18th century artisans, History Alive! portrays the people who fought and lived at Fort Ligonier during the Forbes Campaign of 1758.This educational program is made possible by a #PreservingAmerica grant from Americana Corner.

events.title: Natural Dyeing: Eco-Printing with Fall Leaves w/ Kelly Lane
events.description: Create Wearable Art from Nature in this beginner-friendly natural-dyeing workshop! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Time: 2pm-5pm Description: Join us in the Beth Wainwright Dye Lab at Contemporary Craft for a morning of learning with Kelly Lane, who will guide participants through the process of eco-printing, a method of transferring the shapes and marks of leaves and flowers onto fabric. And, create a uniquely printed, organic cotton bandana! In this workshop, we will capture the autumnal season by exploring the art of eco-printing, where the natural shapes of leaves and flowers are permanently transferred onto fabric through a process of bundling and steaming. We will cover various eco-printing techniques, focusing on a method that combines tannin-soaked fabric and an iron blanket to create rich, moody greys and the negative shapes of leaves. Tannins and iron are materials used to help the printing process. In the workshop, we will also talk more about these materials and where you might acquire them for future at-home printing. You can expect to learn how to prepare fabric and use a special technique to achieve clear, crisp prints. Your one-of-a-kind design will be created on an 18”, organic cotton bandana – the perfect accessory to enliven your fall wardrobe, or to give as a gift during the holiday season. At the end of the workshop, you will be given a project packet that includes details about the eco-printing process along with resources for repeating this method at home. All materials will be provided, but if you would like to bring your own leaves or other plant matter, please feel free to do so. This workshop is open to all skill levels – no prior experience is needed! Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee Registration: Register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application can be found here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Kelly is a natural dye and mixed media artist and educator. Her work is inspired by our innate connection to the natural world and the wellspring of wisdom that surfaces when we slow down and tune in to our surroundings. As an artist, she taps into this connection to create work that is an intermingled reflection of landscapes within and without. For each project, Kelly thoughtfully forages plants to create botanical palettes that imbue both formal beauty and conceptual depth. In addition to plant-based dyes, she also incorporates sustainable or rescued textiles in her work. With over 15 years of experience as a sustainable clothing designer, Kelly has a deep appreciation for natural fibers and the warmth they radiate. In addition to her artistic practice, Kelly loves sharing her passion for creating color with plants through teaching natural dye and ink-making workshops.

events.title: Piano Lumière: Halloween
events.description: Piano Lumière: HalloweenJoin pianists Jimmy Liu and Kevin Lee Sun for Piano Lumière: Halloween, a two-piano concert presented in an intimate setting surrounded by thousands of glowing candles at Duquesne University's PNC Recital Hall. This program features music written for two pianos, including Rachmaninoff's electrifying Tarantella, Saint-Saëns' evocative Danse Macabre, Bach's famously recognizable Toccata, Liszt's Totentanz in a rare version for three pianos, and more. The program will also spotlight the talents of youth pianist Thomas Ngan, Duquesne faculty member Nathália Kato Giordano, and Duquesne student Zoey Wolfe.Set against a luminous autumn atmosphere, Piano Lumière offers an evening of compelling music, from beloved favorites to virtuosic masterworks.PerformancesSaturday, October 17, 2026 – 7:00 PMSunday, October 18, 2026 – 3:00 PM Runtime- 75 minutes

events.title: Haunted Pittsburgh presents: The Haunted Pierogi
events.description: It’s the gilded age of ragtime, robber barons, and boastful mansions bathed in gaslight. Beloved Pittsburgh businessman George Westinghouse, at great personal risk, has conducted an investigation of supernatural phenomena in the Pittsburgh region. His findings were so shocking that he threw it in the fire and never spoke of it again. The world assumed that his findings were gone forever. Until now.The Haunted Pittsburgh Players have obtained the charred manuscript, and they bring the stories to life. It’s The Haunted Pierogi—a hilarious, raucous mash-up of Pittsburgh’s greatest tales of the unexplained. Join Andrew Carnegie, HJ Heinz, Henry Clay Frick, Nikola Tesla…and Jack the Ripper.Pittsburgh has a North Side and a South Side, if you dare, we’ll take you to the dark side. A one night only event!

events.title: The Yeoman of the Guard
events.description:
The Yeomen of the Guard; or, The Merryman and His Maid is set within the Tower of London during the 16th century, where love, loyalty, and deception intertwine beneath the shadow of the executioner’s axe. Colonel Fairfax, a nobleman unjustly condemned to die, devises an unexpected plan to preserve his inheritance, drawing the spirited strolling singer Elsie Maynard and the Tower’s colorful inhabitants into a web of disguises, mistaken identities, and romantic entanglements. As comedy gives way to moments of genuine tenderness and heartbreak, The Yeomen of the Guard explores themes of honor, sacrifice, and the unpredictable nature of love in one of Gilbert & Sullivan’s most emotionally resonant works.

The Yeomen of the Guard is Gilbert & Sullivan’s eleventh collaboration, and premiered in October 1888 at the Savoy Theatre in London. While it retains the wit and memorable melodies for which the pair are celebrated, the opera is distinguished by its richer emotional depth and more serious dramatic tone, making it one of the most unique operettas in the canon.

events.title: In Dead by Ten: Heaven & Hell
events.description:
Arise! It’s time for the third-annual In Dead by Ten Halloween Dance Party, presented by Hidden Harbor, THIS IS RED, and In Bed by Ten, returning on Saturday, October 17 to the stunning, century-old former Slovakian Catholic church that serves as THIS IS RED’s home base and event space in Munhall. Tickets are on sale NOW!

This year’s edition takes on a Heaven & Hell theme, with two levels of DJ’s offering two different dance experiences. Upstairs in the main hall “Pop Heaven,” Slim tha DJ and DJ MB will take you higher, while downstairs in the Disco Dungeon, DJ’s EZ Lou, Buscrates, and Formosa will light a fire under your feet.

Pay a visit to the Tarot Grotto with Tenorina for a frightfully good reading. And don’t forget the costume contest, now with a dance line at 9 p.m. to show off your moves with prizes for Best Group Costume, Best Presentation, and Most Creative. Be an angel, a devil, or both!

Throughout the multiple levels of the space, enjoy diabolically good tropical cocktails, beer, and wine from Hidden Harbor, Independent Brewing Company, Lorelei, and Golden Age, with eats by GA.

All past versions of this event have sold out ahead of the event date, so gather your crew and get your tickets now, with early-bird pricing now thru September 18. And special thanks to @rojowashere for concept and brainstorming!

CLOACA

w/ Kha'dj, Lemon Line, Cereza, LowIron (Philly), Clark Price

Date: October 17, 2026
Time: 9:00 PM – 5:00 AM

Tickets: $20/25/30

Admission: 18+

Once upon a late nite bleary, while I wandered, fog so eerie,
Over many a dull and fiending individual of brainless bore—
    While I shivered, nearly flaking, suddenly there came a quaking,
As of ev'ry one gently shaking, shaking ass at the warehouse door.
"'tis One Whole," I marveled, "quaking at the warehouse door—
    just One Hole and nothing more."

events.title: The Jayhawks
events.description: The Jayhawks are an acclaimed American rock band whose signature blend of Americana, alternative country, folk, and roots rock has made them one of the most influential groups in the alt-country movement. Formed in Minneapolis, the band earned widespread praise through landmark albums such as Hollywood Town Hall, Tomorrow the Green Grass, Rainy Day Music, and Paging Mr. Proust, showcasing exceptional songwriting, rich vocal harmonies, and timeless melodies. Led by the creative partnership of Gary Louris and longtime collaborators, The Jayhawks have built a catalog that explores themes of love, memory, hope, change, and life's quiet moments with poetic lyricism and understated beauty. Their live performances are celebrated for their warm harmonies, accomplished musicianship, and effortless chemistry, creating an intimate atmosphere that resonates with both longtime fans and new listeners. Through decades of artistic evolution and a steadfast commitment to heartfelt songwriting, The Jayhawks continue to stand among the most respected and enduring bands in contemporary Americana and roots music.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.
