events.description: Learn the basics of wood shop machines, processes, and safety in this introductory course! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: This designed-for-beginners course will explore the basics of woodworking in a judgement-free environment! Using the core machines of the wood studio, students will learn the lumber milling process—turning a rough-sawn board into dimensional lumber—which is the launching pad for nearly every wood project. Folks will build familiarity with the studio space, tools, and safety considerations and will walk away with several sample pieces demonstrating knowledge and confidence in the woodshop. If you’re hesitant to jump into one of our project-based workshops or curious if woodworking is even right for you, this is a great place to start! Tuition: $80 + $20 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist David’s love for woodcrafting started as a child when he served as a carving and painting artist’s apprentice to his grandfather in the upstate Finger lakes region of New York. He studied stagecraft, theatre, and construction at Point Park University’s Conservatory of Performing Arts, trained at the KML Carpenters school through the Carpentry Union, and Woodworking fundamentals through the Backchannel School of woodworking; all studied here in Pittsburgh. Since 2021, he has been the owner of the small Pittsburgh based wood working business, Uncommon Craftsmen; and when he’s not at work you can find him under a pile of sawdust, clay, paints, or design drafts problem solving his way through his old Observatory Hill fixer-upper. David is also an avid boardgame enthusiast, a songwriter, and the proud father of two kiddos!

events.title: Movements w/ Balance & Composure
events.description: Movements with Balance and Composure, Midrift, and Niis brings together a powerful lineup of emotionally driven alternative rock, post-hardcore, and shoegaze-inspired acts. Movements are known for blending melodic post-hardcore with introspective lyrics, atmospheric guitar work, and emotionally intense performances that explore themes of mental health, relationships, and personal struggle. Their dynamic sound balances heavy emotional weight with soaring melodies and passionate live energy.Balance and Composure add a moody alternative rock style rooted in post-hardcore, grunge, and shoegaze influences. The band is celebrated for emotionally raw songwriting, layered instrumentation, and immersive performances that create a deeply atmospheric concert experience.Midrift contributes a dreamy and distorted shoegaze sound filled with hazy guitar textures, emotional vulnerability, and modern alternative influences. Their music creates a cinematic atmosphere that complements the heavier emotional tones of the lineup.Niis rounds out the bill with an aggressive punk-infused energy driven by raw vocals, fast-paced instrumentation, and rebellious intensity. Their gritty sound adds a fierce edge to the show, creating a diverse and emotionally charged lineup that spans alternative rock, punk, and post-hardcore music.

events.title: Bob Schneider
events.description: Bob Schneider is an Austin-based singer-songwriter celebrated for a genre-blending sound that brings together alternative rock, folk, funk, country, and pop. A longtime fixture of Austin’s live-music community, he first gained national attention as a solo artist with albums including Lonelyland and I’m Good Now. Schneider’s performances pair a distinctive, husky voice with sharp storytelling, adventurous arrangements, and an engaging sense of humor, creating an experience that can move effortlessly from heartfelt ballads to groove-driven rock. His catalog offers an eclectic introduction to one of Texas’ most distinctive contemporary songwriters.

Known for energetic performances and an authentic artistic voice, he has quickly built a dedicated following within the modern alternative rock scene.

events.title: Mike Dawes (21+ Event)
events.description: Mike Dawes is an acclaimed fingerstyle guitarist known for his extraordinary technical ability, innovative playing techniques, and captivating solo acoustic performances. His music transforms a single guitar into a full-band experience through the use of intricate tapping, percussive rhythms, harmonics, and melodic arrangements. Dawes has gained international recognition for his inventive interpretations of popular songs as well as original compositions that showcase both virtuosity and musical artistry. Known for engaging live performances and a masterful command of the instrument, Mike Dawes is widely regarded as one of the leading figures in contemporary acoustic guitar music.

events.title: Words & Pictures: Kelly Yang
events.description: Mia Tang has a lot of secrets.Number 1: She lives in a motel, not a big house. Every day, while her immigrant parents clean the rooms, ten-year-old Mia manages the front desk of the Calivista Motel and tends to its guests.Number 2: Her parents hide immigrants. And if the mean motel owner, Mr. Yao, finds out they’ve been letting them stay in the empty rooms for free, the Tangs will be doomed.Number 3: She wants to be a writer. But how can she when her mom thinks she should stick to math because English is not her first language?It will take all of Mia’s courage, kindness, and hard work to get through this year. Will she be able to hold on to her job, help the immigrants and guests, escape Mr. Yao, and pursue her writing dreams?Kelly Yang is the New York Times bestselling, award-winning author of the Front Desk series, winner of the 2019 Asian Pacific American Award for Children’s Literature. Her books include Front Desk, Three Keys, Room to Dream, Parachutes, New From Here, and other middle grade and young adult novels. She was born in China and grew up in Los Angeles. She went to college at the age of 13 and graduated from UC Berkeley at the age of 17 and Harvard Law School at the age of 20. After law school, she founded The Kelly Yang Project, a writing and debating program for children in Asia. Prior to becoming a novelist, she wrote for many years for the South China Morning Post, The New York Times, The Washington Post, and The Atlantic. She lives in Los Angeles with her family.

events.title: Natural Dyeing: Eco-Printing with Fall Leaves w/ Kelly Lane
events.description: Create Wearable Art from Nature in this beginner-friendly natural-dyeing workshop! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Thursday, October 22, 2026 Time: 6pm -9pm Description: Join us in the Beth Wainwright Dye Lab at Contemporary Craft for a morning of learning with Kelly Lane, who will guide participants through the process of eco-printing, a method of transferring the shapes and marks of leaves and flowers onto fabric. And, create a uniquely printed, organic cotton bandana! In this workshop, we will capture the autumnal season by exploring the art of eco-printing, where the natural shapes of leaves and flowers are permanently transferred onto fabric through a process of bundling and steaming. We will cover various eco-printing techniques, focusing on a method that combines tannin-soaked fabric and an iron blanket to create rich, moody greys and the negative shapes of leaves. Tannins and iron are materials used to help the printing process. In the workshop, we will also talk more about these materials and where you might acquire them for future at-home printing. You can expect to learn how to prepare fabric and use a special technique to achieve clear, crisp prints. Your one-of-a-kind design will be created on an 18”, organic cotton bandana – the perfect accessory to enliven your fall wardrobe, or to give as a gift during the holiday season. At the end of the workshop, you will be given a project packet that includes details about the eco-printing process along with resources for repeating this method at home. All materials will be provided, but if you would like to bring your own leaves or other plant matter, please feel free to do so. This workshop is open to all skill levels – no prior experience is needed! Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee Registration: Register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application can be found here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Kelly is a natural dye and mixed media artist and educator. Her work is inspired by our innate connection to the natural world and the wellspring of wisdom that surfaces when we slow down and tune in to our surroundings. As an artist, she taps into this connection to create work that is an intermingled reflection of landscapes within and without. For each project, Kelly thoughtfully forages plants to create botanical palettes that imbue both formal beauty and conceptual depth. In addition to plant-based dyes, she also incorporates sustainable or rescued textiles in her work. With over 15 years of experience as a sustainable clothing designer, Kelly has a deep appreciation for natural fibers and the warmth they radiate. In addition to her artistic practice, Kelly loves sharing her passion for creating color with plants through teaching natural dye and ink-making workshops.

events.title: Soiree in the Strip
events.description: The Midwife Center's fourth annual Soiree in the Strip is Thursday, October 22, 2026 at Heinz History Center! A celebration of Southwestern Pennsylvania's only licensed, freestanding birth center, Soiree in the Strip brings together local leaders, clients, and community to raise critical funds for The Midwife Center's programs and services.Guests will enjoy a light dinner buffet, desserts, drinks, a silent auction & raffle, trivia, and exclusive, after-hours access to museum exhibits. Soiree in the Strip is chaired and emceed by journalist Natalie Bencivenga.The Midwife Center promotes wellness by providing exceptional, client-centered primary gynecological, pregnancy and birthing care in southwestern Pennsylvania’s only independent birth center.5:30-7 PM - VIP Reception - Doors open at 5:30 PM for VIP guests to enjoy extra time exploring Heinz History Center. Join us for elevated hors d'oeuvres & exclusive exhibit tours throughout the reception.7-8:30 PM - Main Event - Enjoy a light dinner buffet, desserts, trivia, and a silent auction and raffle. The brief program, auction, and raffle drawing will conclude by 8:30 PM.8:30-9:30 PM - After Party - Keep the fun going and get extended after-hours exhibit access.Don’t miss out on this special celebration to raise critical funds for The Midwife Center's compassionate, evidence-based primary gynecological, prenatal, birthing, and postpartum care.

events.title: Michael Misko in Once Upon a Midnight
events.description: Beneath the bridges and the brick, Pittsburgh is alive with whispers of stories that never quite died.This October, Liberty Magic transforms into something darker, closer, and far more personal.In this world premiere experience, Michael steps into a more serious, story‑driven role inviting you into an intimate evening of Pittsburgh folk tales, ghost lore, and haunted history. This is not the Michael you’ve seen before.Set against the backdrop of Halloween season, Michael weaves chilling stories of our city’s past brought to life through unusual magic, mysterious artifacts, and strange heirlooms. The experience unfolds less like a traditional magic show and more like interactive theater, where you’re not just watching the story; you’re part of it.Liberty Magic is known for being up close, but this goes even further. Expect a shared, immersive atmosphere that feels like a late‑night storytelling circle, where the line between performer and audience is the first thing to disappear. Once that's gone, all bets are off."The Steel City has a haunted past. Tonight...it gets a voice."

events.title: Jordan Jensen
events.description: Jordan Jensen is a stand-up comedian known for fearless humor, quick crowd work, and an unapologetically raw comedic style that blends personal storytelling with sharp observational comedy. Her performances often explore relationships, social awkwardness, mental health, and everyday absurdities through brutally honest punchlines and high-energy delivery. Jensen has gained recognition for her fast-rising presence in the comedy scene, earning attention through podcast appearances, live performances, and viral stand-up clips that showcase her edgy and unpredictable humor. With bold stage presence and a conversational comedic approach, Jordan Jensen has become one of the emerging voices in modern stand-up comedy.

events.title: Emma Nissen
events.description: Emma Nissen is an American singer-songwriter known for her self-described “Christian Jazz” style, combining soulful vocals, jazz influences, gospel melodies and faith-centered songwriting. She gained recognition after a 2023 Instagram reel featuring “Breathe” went viral. Her debut album, Love Like You (2024), reached No. 1 on the iTunes Christian music chart within 24 hours of release. Nissen’s 2026 album, Moved, includes “Lovin’,” “Live and Let Live” and “So Much Love in My Heart.”

events.title: Candlebox with Sponge
events.description: Candlebox: Candlebox emerged during the early 1990s rock explosion with a powerful blend of grunge, hard rock, and melodic songwriting that quickly earned the band a devoted following. Led by vocalist Kevin Martin, the group broke through with a self-titled debut album featuring enduring fan favorites that remain staples of rock radio and live performances. Over the years, Candlebox has continued to evolve while preserving the emotional intensity, soaring vocals, and guitar-driven sound that first made them stand out. Concertgoers can expect an energetic performance packed with classic hits, deep album cuts, and the passionate musicianship that has kept the band a fixture on rock stages for more than three decades.Sponge: Sponge has been a mainstay of alternative rock since the mid-1990s, earning recognition for its driving guitar riffs, memorable hooks, and the unmistakable vocals of frontman Vinnie Dombroski. The band's catalog combines hard-edged rock with melodic influences, producing songs that have become favorites among fans of the era while continuing to attract new listeners. Through consistent touring and new releases, Sponge has maintained its reputation as a dynamic live act capable of delivering both nostalgic anthems and fresh material with equal intensity. Their concerts showcase powerful performances, infectious energy, and a polished stage presence that highlights the band's enduring impact on the alternative rock landscape.

events.title: Low Cut Connie
events.description: Low Cut Connie is the Philadelphia rock & roll project led by pianist, songwriter, and frontman Adam Weiner. The band’s piano-driven sound blends raw early rock, boogie, and sharp, danceable songwriting, with influences ranging from Jerry Lee Lewis to the Rolling Stones. Low Cut Connie gained wider recognition after “Boozophilia” appeared on Barack Obama’s 2015 summer playlist. Notable releases include the debut album Get Out the Lotion, Private Lives, and the 2026 album Livin in the USA, featuring songs such as “Can’t Be Wrong,” “Oh Yeah,” and “Little Freakers.”

events.title: LIVE
events.description:
What makes a live set live?

“LIVE” plays with that question, bringing together Pittsburgh artists who compose, improvise, and reimagine music in real time.

From experimental and downtempo performances to live coding and creative manipulation of existing tracks, our first event explores different approaches to electronic music and the many ways it can take shape in front of an audience.

Some things are planned, some things happen in the moment, and that’s part of the fun.

A little experimentation, a little improvisation, and plenty of room to groove.

events.title: Othello of the End Zone, or The Steel City Tragedy
events.description:
Step onto the 50-yard line for the New Hazlett’s first-ever co-production with DEMASKUS Theater Collective: Othello of the End Zone, or The Steel City Tragedy. Written by Franky D. Gonzalez, directed by Shaunda Miles McDill, and starring Cynthia Dallas and Michael Patrick Trimm, this high-stakes modern reimagining brings Shakespeare to the Northside stage. When Imani Othello is named Head Coach of America's most beloved football franchise, the pressure mounts on and off the field. This hard-hitting adaptation centers a Black woman calling the plays at the height of her power, confronting ambition, betrayal, and relentless doubt.
•	Dates: October 22–24 at 7:30 PM | October 24 at 2:00 PM | October 25 at 3:00 PM
•	Tickets: $50 (Thursday, Oct. 22: Pay-What-You-Can starting at $20)
•	Purchase: https://ci.ovationtix.com/36406/production/1291006

events.title: Claudio Simonetti's Goblin: Tenebre Live Score
events.description: Claudio Simonetti's Goblin comes to Pittsburgh's Thunderbird Music Hall on October 22nd for a landmark event: a live performance of their iconic score to Dario Argento's 1982 giallo horror masterpiece 'Tenebre,' performed live in sync with a full screening of the film. The evening will also feature a set of classic hits from Goblin's legendary catalog, spanning their work on Suspiria, Deep Red, Dawn of the Dead, and more. Goblin is the Italian progressive rock band whose film scores defined the sound of Italian horror cinema in the 1970s and 80s. Claudio Simonetti, the band's founding keyboardist and primary composer, leads this incarnation of the group. Promoted by Tone Deaf Touring. Find more at: soundcloud.com/claudio-simonetti

Watch our set take shape, create a costume piece, make a community art piece, and go behind the curtain like never before.Your $50 ticket includes wine tasting, light bites, live entertainment, and behind-the-scenes activities.Sip & Sing is hosted at the Bitz Opera Factory’s Hahn Rehearsal Hall and Costume Shop – areas not usually open to the public!

events.title: All Them Witches
events.description: All Them Witches is a Nashville-based quartet known for its immersive blend of bluesy, neo-psychedelic rock, stoner metal and progressive space rock. Their music balances heavy, fuzz-drenched grooves with spacious arrangements, melodic detail and an atmospheric sense of mystery. The band’s current creative chapter centers on *House of Mirrors*, a 2026 full-length album that explores dark, introspective themes while showcasing the group’s evolving sound. Audiences can expect a powerful, richly textured concert experience shaped by electric guitar, bass, drums, keyboards and expressive vocals.

events.title: Joe Stamm Band w/ Josh Travis
events.description: VIP event 6PM (Tickets available through Joe Stamm website)Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$20 ADV | Show $25Joe Stamm has a way of making seemingly minor moments feel as expansive and full as the Illinois River that runs through his central Illinois homeland. As Joe continues building a life in that same river valley, new stories continue revealing themselves to him. In the sound of the crickets on a summer night. In the smell of bonfire smoke on a mild winter day. In the taste of a cold garage beer.After more than a decade of writing, performing, and touring, Stamm has honed his storytelling ability to such fine detail, youd think he was there when you were getting up to no good in your hometown. Or at your dinner table when you got the bad news. Or on your porch when you got the good news. His salt-of-the-earth writing style, coupled with a voice that urges you to feel deeplywell, thats what honest music is all about.Pennsylvania singer-songwriter Josh Travis carries listeners on a captivating journey through hisrestless spirit. With its title alone, his debut full-length album, Few of Days & Full of Trouble evokesa range of familiar emotions.His deeply personal lyrics sown across accessible themes bear the hallmarks of an honest andapproachable songwriter.

Joining him on tour, Fridayy brings his own unique blend of soulful vocals, songwriting talent, and contemporary R&B influences, earning widespread recognition through collaborations with major artists as well as his successful solo work. Together, Rod Wave and Fridayy deliver a compelling combination of raw emotion, melodic artistry, and authentic storytelling that has helped shape the sound of today's hip-hop and R&B landscape.

events.title: Night of Death & Disaster
events.description:
Join us for our annual Halloween celebration, a Night of Death and Disaster! Come dressed in your best macabre couture as we dive deep into Warhol’s darker side for a night of eerie revelry, but help us protect our collection. No masks, wings, tails or other props that could bump the artwork.

-DJ set by Second Skin (Erica Scary & Huck Finn)
-Tarot readings by Three3Three and Pgh Astrology
-Take home your own spooky poems typed on a typewriter live by Sprouts of Consciousness
-Floral arrangements and decor by greenSinner
-Stay tuned: More mayhem to be announced!
-Please note: This event is for ages 21+.

This celebration sold out last year. Don’t miss out.

In his "Death and Disaster" series, Warhol explored the impact of images taken out of a journalistic context and framed, through repetition, as works of art. Some of the photographs that Warhol chose as source images for this series depict horrific scenes. Others focus on a narrative that may not be obvious, but is symbolic of death and disaster nonetheless, such as the Electric Chair and Jackie series. In all of these works, Warhol repeated images to mirror the repetition evident in society through media and technology.

Night of Death and Disaster is sponsored by Design Within Reach.

events.title: Drawing & Mark Making on Enamel with Andrew Thornton
events.description: Learn to embellish your enameled surfaces with drawing & mark making techniques! 7-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 24th Time: 10am-5pm Description: Enameling is a method of bonding glass to metal. It is a wonderful way to add color and vibrancy to your creations. In this class, we’ll be going one step further and exploring mark making and drawing on enameled surfaces. We will cover the different ways to prepare the drawing surfaces, go over what products will work to create your illustrations (and which ones won’t), and discuss finishing touches. This is great for 2D artists looking to put their artwork on jewelry or anyone looking to make their enameled pieces stand out. Not confident in drawing? That’s okay! events.title: SPECIAL TOUR: HISTORIC THORNBURG, PA
events.description: Saturday, October 24, 202610:00 am to 12:00 pm$25.00 per personRising on a bluff above the valley carved by the Chartiers Creek, the Borough of Thornburg is a little piece of Southern California in southwestern Pennsylvania. The planned suburb was created in 1899 by Frank Thornburg and his cousin David on land that had been in the family since 1806. Early houses built here were in the Queen Anne Style. By 1904, however, the Pittsburgh Gazette celebrated the "model and aristocratic suburb" for its "most unique collection of houses near Pittsburgh." The variety of historical residential styles would soon be augmented by homes inspired by Frank Thornburg's personal passion: the contemporary Mission-and Craftsman-style houses he saw and studied during travels in Los Angeles and vicinity. With a willing accomplice in his cousin, architect Samuel McClarren, Thornburg would create an enclave that still retains its architectural and natural integrity and that continues to delight with its tough of SoCal style.

events.title: Natural Dye Workshop: Indigo (Fold, Clamp, Resist) with Amy Garbark
events.description: Become familiar with the incredible plant, Japanese Indigo (persicaria tinctoria) and create a sweet gift in the process! Natural Dye Workshop: Indigo (Fold, Clamp, Resist) with Amy Garbark Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Time: 10am-1pm Description: In this beginner friendy workshop, participants will become familiar with the incredible plant, Japanese Indigo (persicaria tinctoria) in a small group setting. Indigo has been used to dye textiles for thousands of years! Workshop participants will learn about indigo and a variety of shibori techniques to prepare fabric for dyeing in a natural indigo vat. Shibori is a process of creating patterns on fabric through processes of folding, binding, and clamping (and more!) and dyeing. The shape created by the folds and clamps create a beautiful blue and white pattern when dyed in indigo. Participants will then dip the prepared and folded fabric into the indigo vat and repeat the process of dipping and oxidizing until the desired depth of blue is achieved, before unbinding our beautiful fabrics! Workshop participants will be able to choose between a variety of materials for dyeing: bandana, pillowcase, cloth napkins, etc. Participants may also bring 1 x article of clothing, fabric, etc. from home to dye. All fabric should be 100% natural fiber like cotton or linen and washed thoroughly. Each participant will go home with their own custom made, unique, indigo dyed piece! events.title: Beginner Woodworking: Steelers Flight Board with John Henley
events.description: Celebrate the return of Fall Football Season by making a custom Pittsburgh-themed flight board! (just in time for the France Game!) 4-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Time: 11am–3pm Description: Make your Pittsburgh-themed flight board! Students will explore the foundations of woodworking – from milling a slab into a project board, to dowel joints, to finishing a fun custom project. First, we’ll mill a rough-sawn board into surfaced lumber. Then, we’ll add dowel feet and drill holes for drinking glass. Finally, students will choose from a variety of Pittsburgh-themed engraved coasters to inlay into their boards, from our sports teams to Jalapeno Hannah to an Eat’n’Park cookie – only Pittsburgh icons! Come with no woodworking experience and leave with a handmade souvenir celbrating your favorite sports team! Tuition: $90 + $25 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. About the Artist John Henley is a woodworker, designer, and researcher who creates functional objects that build connection with the materials, landscapes, and people surrounding us. John received a B.Des in Industrial Design from Carnegie Mellon University and served as an apprentice for master woodworker Tadao Arimoto. Having grown up in Oregon and now based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, John’s interest in the landscape—both natural and built—impacts his work, which combines traditional craft practices and contemporary praxis. John has received multiple awards and residencies, including a fellowship with the Steve Jobs Archive and, currently, an apprenticeship with Contemporary Craft, where he is supporting arts education while maintaining a studio practice.

events.description: Mike Super – Magic and Illusion: Mike Super is an award-winning illusionist and entertainer renowned for blending astonishing magic with humor, audience participation, and captivating storytelling. Rising to national prominence through his appearances on television talent competitions and magic specials, he has earned a reputation for creating performances that combine grand illusions with intimate moments that leave audiences questioning what they just witnessed. Rather than relying solely on visual spectacle, Super's shows emphasize personal connection, weaving comedy, suspense, and interactive demonstrations into an experience that appeals to families and magic enthusiasts alike. Fans attending a Mike Super performance can expect an unforgettable evening filled with mind-bending illusions, impossible feats, and engaging moments that transform spectators into active participants in the magic.

events.title: Noel Paul Stookey
events.venue_name: Carnegie Music Hall of Oakland - Pittsburgh
events.description: Noel Paul Stookey is an acclaimed singer-songwriter best known as the “Paul” of the legendary folk trio Peter, Paul and Mary. His solo performances draw on a remarkable catalog that includes “The Wedding Song (There Is Love),” alongside folk, jazz, spiritual, and socially conscious music. Stookey describes his distinctive blend of folk lyrics and jazz improvisation as “fazz,” a style showcased throughout his solo work. A longtime advocate for social change, he continues to connect music with messages of justice, inclusion, hope, and community action.

events.title: SkyWatch: Life on Moons
events.description: Is there anyone out there? Uncover how NASA has looked for key elements of life on moons in our solar systems and how the Cassini mission contributed to these efforts. Draw an extreme environment beyond Earth and invent a living thing that could survive there, modeling NASA scientists’ study on extremophiles. Build a spacecraft and put it through a series of tests to ensure it’s ready to launch. Additionally, enjoy a planetarium show and stargazing time on the observatory deck (weather-permitting). Viewing targets include Saturn, the Moon, and Pleiades, an open star cluster located about 440 light-years away in the constellation Taurus.

events.title: 2 SQUARE IMPROV
events.description: We couldnt be more excited to welcome 2 Square to the bottlerocket stage especially after seeing their amazing set this year ar UCB's DCM 26'. Two of the best John Lutz and Peter Grosz take a single suggestion then spin that into a longform show featuring a kaleidoscope of scenes, absurdist transitional elements and callbacks – all while never once using a “sweep edit” to get from scene to scene. John Lutz has been acting, improvising and writing for over 30 years. You may know him best as Lutz from 30 Rock. Other screen appearances include: Loot, Girls5Eva, Chicago Med, The Good Wife and Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt. Film credits include The Comedian, Sisters and Sleepwalk with Me. He wrote for Saturday Night Live from 2004-2010 and is currently in his 12th year writing for Late Night with Seth Meyers. For 3 years, he toured the world from Bangkok to Rockford, IL with The Second City National Touring Company. He recently wrote the NY Times bestselling audiobook Escape from Virtual Island. He created, co-wrote and produced the series Mapleworth Murders with Paula Pell,which is streaming on Roku. Peter Grosz has been teaching improvisation and writing at various theaters across America for the last 25 years. He wrote and performed in four reviews with The Second City ETC and was a founding member of the experimental improv groups JTS Brown, 4 Square and 2 Square. He has written for The Colbert Report, Late Night With Seth Meyers and At Home With Amy Sedaris, winning two Emmys, three WGA awards and a Peabody along the way. You’ve seen him in The Menu, Veep, The Bear, The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, The President Show and more. You can hear him on Wait Wait, Don’t Tell Me on NPR and he was in a few commercials for Sonic drive-in, but only for 18 years so you might have missed them. Seating/Show Information: This show will have theater seating. Seats will be assigned upon arrival, or can be chosen ahead of time for an additional fee. QR Code Ordering will be available for this performance. Doors open at 9pm. Don't miss our famous Bottlerocket Pre-Show Clip Collection, beginning one hour before the start of the performance. This show is ALL AGES *all information subject to change as needed. Bottlerocket FAQ: All shows starting before 10pm are all ages unless otherwise noted. Free parking is available at 824 Industry Street and 205 Allen Street, as well as other public lots in the area. Live Music shows have limited seating options, please arrive early or reach out to the venue directly if you know that you require a seat. Doors open at 5pm for all shows unless noted otherwise. The time listed on the ticket is the event's true start time. Most shows have a preshow experience starting 1 hour before the show. Our full refund policy can be viewed here Please contact us ahead of time with any accesibilty requests or concerns, we're happy to accomodate you. More FAQ's can be found here

Bliss will take you from Arizona to London and from heartbreak to elation with her lyrics, all while merging Old-Time melodies with Bluegrass moments. A New Yorker by birth and a Texan at heart, she sings with occasional omission of vowels and consistent Southern charm.

events.title: The Lowest Pair
events.description: Doors 6PM | Show 7PM$15 ADV | $20 DOSThe Lowest PairThe Lowest Pair has questions. The duo, made up of Kendl Winter and Palmer T. Lee, know that we tend to see duality as a problem. We want life to be linear, working through the dark to finally get to the light. Grief to joy, despair to hope, confusion to claritynot a jangly cycle we cant escape. But through their incandescent folk songs, the Lowest Pair often ask: What if we sit with the mess? What if thats not just more peaceful, but more magical, too? Fare thee well and go to hell, I love you and Im mad at you. Its such a theme in my life, Winter says, then laughs. Wishing things were different but loving all of it, too.On their 8th album Always As Young As Well Ever Be, the Lowest Pair prove that over the last dozen years together, theyve become some of modern roots musics most mesmerizing, thoughtful purveyors. Produced by Tucker Martine (The Decemberists), the 10-track album puts the duos stark lyricism, string-driven arrangements, and raw compatibility on brilliant display. Were both trying to make space for each other rather than crowd each other out, Lee says, reflecting on why the Lowest Pair works. Were doing a lot of listening and reacting to what the other person is doing. Lees speaking voice is a comforting echo of his singing voice, soft and precise. Winter talks like she sings, too, sweet and raspy. Heard together, the effect is both soothing and scintillating, like a crisp mountain stream smoothing rocks. The Lowest Pairs musicianship is another beautiful testament not just to playing that breathes, but playing that listens. Winter, who grew up in Arkansas but has lived in Washington State for the last two decades, and Lee, a Minnesota native, first gained attention as poetic singer-songwriters on banjos. While their family of strings has expandedWinter plays more guitar on the new record than she ever has beforetheir fundamental approach hasnt: Respond to sounds and stories the other is making.

events.title: Creed Fisher
events.description: Creed Fisher is a West Texas singer-songwriter known for blending traditional country with modern elements and hard-rock influence. His music draws on working-class themes, patriotism and personal experience. Fisher’s notable releases include the albums Old School, which reached No. 3 on the iTunes Country Albums chart, and Hellraiser, which debuted at No. 2. His catalog also includes the songs “I’ll Keep Drinkin’,” “Ain’t Scared to Bleed” and “Fairies Wear Boots,” a cover of the Black Sabbath classic.

events.title: Prayers
events.description: Prayers is a San Diego-based electronic rock duo known for pioneering “cholo goth,” a distinctive fusion of darkwave, goth rock, synth-pop and Mexican-American street culture. Founded by Leafar Seyer and Dave Parley, the project pairs moody synthesizers, throbbing electronic rhythms and introspective vocals with a bold visual identity. Their catalog includes the albums *SD Killwave*, *Young Gods* and *Baptism of Thieves*, along with collaborations connected to Christian Death and other alternative artists. For listeners drawn to atmospheric, boundary-pushing rock and dark electronic music, Prayers offers an immersive performance rooted in self-expression and genre-defying creativity.

events.title: Phillip Phillips
events.description: Phillip Phillips is a platinum-selling singer-songwriter whose warm, soulful voice and blend of folk, rock, pop, and Americana have made him one of the most recognizable artists to emerge from American Idol. After winning the competition's eleventh season, he achieved immediate success with the multi-platinum hit "Home," followed by fan favorites including "Gone, Gone, Gone," "Raging Fire," and "Miles." Known for his heartfelt songwriting and acoustic-driven sound, Phillips draws inspiration from roots rock, blues, and contemporary singer-songwriter traditions, creating music that emphasizes authenticity, resilience, and human connection. His live performances showcase expressive vocals, accomplished guitar playing, and a relaxed stage presence that allows audiences to connect with both his chart-topping singles and deeper album cuts. Through years of touring and consistently evolving as a songwriter, Phillip Phillips has established himself as a respected artist whose timeless melodies and sincere storytelling continue to resonate with fans around the world.

events.title: Ten Evenings: Michael Lewis
events.description: An inside look at the early days of Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency, as told by the public servants it targeted and one of America’s best storytellers.Blockers. It wasn’t a compliment. In the new Washington, it was the worst thing you could be—especially if you worked in the federal government and wanted to keep your job. A Blocker was a holdover, an impediment, someone who didn’t get the message—and, most of all, someone who didn’t belong.Michael Lewis found seven of them.Blockers is the story of people who believed they had a calling, who were convinced they were doing something the country couldn’t do without, and then discovered they were no longer wanted. One kept Americans’ most sensitive tax data out of the wrong hands and another made sure that politicians and civil servants played by the rules. One figured out how to stop wildfires from destroying suburban neighborhoods, another helped uncover the mysteries of cystic fibrosis.There was also a security guard.It should come as no surprise that the writer who made subprime mortgages gripping (The Big Short) and who turned baseball statistics into poetry (Moneyball) could transform the first two years of the second Trump administration into a thriller about federal employees. But he does.And he does something else. He puts before us a clear question: If these public servants can’t survive in government today, then what does that say about us?New York Times bestselling author Michael Lewis has published many books on subjects ranging from politics to Wall Street. Lewis’s most recent #1 New York Times bestselling book, Going Infinite, tells the story of FTX’s collapse and the enigmatic founder at its center, Sam Bankman-Fried.Lewis is the creator and host of Apple’s #1 rated podcast Against the Rules, a searing look at what’s happened to fairness in American life through the lens of people who depend on public trust.Mr. Lewis grew up in New Orleans and remains deeply interested and involved in the city. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Art History from Princeton and a Master’s degree in Economics from the London School of Economics. He lives in Berkeley, California, with his wife, Tabitha Soren, and their children.

events.title: Hadestown - The Musical - Pittsburgh, PA
events.description: COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go.

Together, these performers create a diverse concert experience that highlights the continued evolution of modern rock while delivering the passion and intensity that fans have come to expect from the genre.

events.title: Spirits of Hallowe'en History Tours
events.description: Step into the shadows this Hallowe'en at West Overton Village & Museum! Explore the eerie origins of Halloween traditions from ancient Celtic rituals to Victorian parties and today's trick or treat. Uncover the dark and fascinating history behind your favorite haunted holiday. Local Halloween celebrations once spanned days of frightful fun. Learn about the debauchery of Chalk Night and Mischief Night across southwestern Pennsylvania. Hear true tales of neighborhood pranks from the ever-popular “corning” to more dangerous hijinks: wheelbarrows hanging from telephone poles, signs missing from buildings, and entire wagons hoisted onto roofs. Tour the 1838 Overholt Homestead by candlelight. Try some Victorian fortune telling party games: Who will be your future love? Will you become wealthy? Who in your group will meet an untimely demise?Stop by a re-created 1800s Halloween party and enjoy a variety of historical treats. Written using dozens of local newspaper articles and historical sources, this immersive tour delves into the real history of Hallow’s Eve.Plan your visitTours are available at 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, and 7:30 on October 28, 29, and 30.Each tour is approximately one hour and involves walking outdoors, up and down stairs, and in the dark. Please register in advance - tours have limited capacity and we cannot guarantee there will be tickets available at the door.

events.title: Rigid Heddle Weaving Series: Texture, Lace, and Fancies w/ Sam Adioetomo
events.description: Learn how to weave with a rigid heddle loom—a portable and playful table top loom — and make a wearable, totable work of art! 4-Part Series Workshop! Date: Thursdays October 29 – November 19, 2026! 6-9pm Description: Over 4 delightful evenings, students will learn how to work with a rigid heddle loom! A rigid heddle loom is a table top loom variation that allows a weaver to create yardage — or designed projects (think scarf, tote bag, table runner, placemat, for example)— while enjoying the meditative potential of this loom. Working with a rigid heddle loom is a great place to start for those who are new to weaving, as well as those who are experienced weavers looking for a portable tool to add to their skill set! Rigid heddle weaving is fun and is welcoming of experimentation right from the start! With Sam’s direction, students will go through all of the steps to using a rigid heddle loom, from dressing it with the warp yarn to taking their weavings off of the loom to create finished pieces! Additionally, Sam will focus specially on techniques to create texture, lace and other fancies If you are looking for a chill, beginner friendly weaving experience, this series might be for you! Students will use the rigid heddle looms in the Contemporary Craft studio, and materials will be provided. However, students will be welcomed to bring any yarn from home that they might like to use. To note: Rigid heddle weaving can be a great way to use up left over bits of yarn from past knitting projects, etc. This class is 100% beginner friendly. No prior experience is necessary or expected. However, this class is also great if you have some experience with weaving on a rigid heddle loom, as Sam will share neat techniques and ways to enhance and add to your weaving repertoire! Tuition: $210 + $20 materials fee Materials: Materials fee includes yarn. Option to purchase a rigid heddle loom through CC will be available too! Registration: Register via Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing on the CC website on your mobile device, please click this link to go to the eventbrite registration page! Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are often available to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. We strive to create a welcoming experience. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the artist: Sam Adioetomo is a knitter, spinner, dyer, and weaver who grew up surrounded by crafters. Her grandmother, Ilene Raycraft, taught her to knit from age seven, and her mother, Kelly Fifield, is a sewist, quilter, singer, and stained-glass artist. Her grandfather, Ray Raycraft, was a stained-glass artist and musician. Sam learned to make yarn on a drop spindle in 2003 at a local yarn shop in Bloomington, Indiana, where she attended university. During the pandemic, she purchased a spinning wheel and picked up spinning techniques from Jillian Eve’s extensive online resources. With an ever-growing stash and a very slow knitting pace, Sam then took up weaving to use up her handspun yarn. In her professional life, Sam works as a writer and, before moving to Pittsburgh, spent most of her career in Indonesia. She sings a lot of shape notes and lives in Edgewood with her husband, three cats, a chihuahua, and a very fluffy rabbit.

events.title: Barbara Kingsolver in conversation with Anna Singer
events.description: The story of a brief, passionate, life-changing love affair, wrapped up in what might be the greatest romance of all: our eternal human longing for art and beauty.Livia Cable has made her peace with her marriage and modest livelihood in the farm country where she grew up, until a shocking phone call from an old lover shakes her to the core. Decades earlier, this man knew her as Livia Bohusz, a music conservatory student estranged from her home and family, uncertain of anything except her passion for music and promise as an extraordinary pianist. His request, now, to see her again stirs up ghosts she’s kept at bay for a lifetime.Shifting between past and present, Livia’s decision to meet or reject the reunion means confronting step by step, in memories framed as musical dances, the experiences of childhood loss, abandonment, self-immolating passion, and perilous attachment to a man who broke her belief in love and ruptured the course of her life.With razor-sharp acuity and deep affection, Pulitzer Prize winner Barbara Kingsolver’s unforgettable new novel reflects on class barriers, the risks of ambition, and the timeless, life-changing power of art.Barbara Kingsolver is the author of ten bestselling works of fiction, including the novels Unsheltered, The Bean Trees, and The Poisonwood Bible, as well as books of poetry, essays, creative nonfiction, and Coyote’s Wild Home, a children’s book co-authored with Lily Kingsolver. She also collaborated with family members on the influential Animal, Vegetable, Miracle: A Year of Food Life. Kingsolver’s work has been translated into more than thirty languages and has earned a devoted readership at home and abroad. She is a member of the American Academy of Arts and Letters, and has received numerous awards and honors including the 2023 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for her novel, Demon Copperhead, the National Humanities Medal, and most recently, the National Book Foundation’s Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters. She lives with her husband on a farm in southern Appalachia.

events.title: Marcedes Carroll & Doc Elliot
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM $15 ADV | $20 DOS 21+ Marcedes Carroll, born in the Rockies and raised in Montana is a resilient, deep-thinking artist with a soulful voice & songs that will cut straight through to the heart of the matter. In 2023 she recorded her second project & first full length record at Bandcamp Recording Studio in Bozeman, Montana. The record, "We Lost track of the Stars," released on September 20th, 2024, and is truly a labor of love. Currently, Marcedes is working on new material for a third project & second full record, playing in a duo & occasional full band with Doc Elliot. Doc Elliot is a singer-songwriter, performer & former touring manager/bandmate with Jaime Wyatt & Kinky Friedman. Originally from Oceanside, CA, he has toured the country since a young age, released multiple records, and been a supporting act for some of the nation's most beloved bands! Their sound is best described as country/singer-songwriter, pulling from '60s/'70s influences such as Patsy Cline, Emmylou Harris, Linda Ronstadt, Willie Nelson, Glen Campbell, Merle Haggard, and many more. The two split time between Southwest Montana, Southern California & Nashville.

events.description: We are embracing Hannibal and horror for “The Silence of the Lambs Cage Night” as our historic building is transformed into two full floors of seasonal entertainment and spooky thrills. While open to all ages, keep in mind the film is rated R and will be screened in its entirety as part of the evening. The heart of this event is a life-sized replica of Hannibal’s cage, complete with a live Hannibal Lecter and the original rug and bed-frame from the film. Who will be brave enough to get a photo with Hannibal, in the same room where the infamous cage scene was filmed…?! Speaking of scary, costumes are encouraged. However, please no full-face masks or weapons. Stroll the vendor marketplace, featuring some of the spookiest merchandise and entertainment in Pittsburgh. A variety of specialty refreshments will be available to purchase, including a cash bar for guests ages 21 and older. If you do intend to partake, please be sure to bring a valid photo ID.

Fans can expect an intimate, heartfelt concert experience rooted in classic R&B while reflecting the realities of contemporary life.

events.description: Dweezil Zappa is an acclaimed guitarist, songwriter and bandleader known for bringing his father Frank Zappa’s adventurous music to the concert stage. His performances blend intricate compositions, jazz-rock fusion, virtuosic guitar work and playful musicality, offering longtime fans and curious newcomers an engaging introduction to the Zappa catalog. In 2026, he is presenting DZ20: Like Father, Like Son, a concert program marking two decades of performing Frank Zappa’s music live. Expect a dynamic, technically impressive rock experience shaped by complex arrangements, sharp musicianship and Dweezil’s distinctive artistic voice.

events.title: Slovak Heritage Festival
events.description: On Sunday, November 1, 2026, from 12:00PM to 4:00PM, the Slovak Studies Program with the help of our generous sponsors will host the 36th Annual Slovak Heritage Festival in the Commons Room of the Cathedral of Learning on the University of Pittsburgh campus in Oakland. We are excited to be back again for a joyous day of Slovak culture, music, history, food and education. At Slovak Fest, you can wander through our vendors and informational display tables, explore the Czechoslovak Room, enjoy a lineup of traditional music and dance performances, attend lectures on Slovak culture, and maybe even meet the ambassador! Admission is free, and parking in Oakland is free on Sundays. The Slavic Languages and Literatures Department at the University of Pittsburgh is proud to be the home of the only permanent Slovak Studies Program in the United States. Our goal is to encourage young people to learn more about Slovakia and the role of Slovaks in America, and to promote and preserve Slovak heritage, language, and culture. There is no better place to do it than right here in Pittsburgh! Thanks to all the organizations and individuals whose combined support has allowed Pitt to serve as a beacon of the Slovak diaspora.

events.title: Grateful Shred
events.description: Grateful Shred is a collective of accomplished musicians dedicated to celebrating the music and improvisational spirit of the Grateful Dead through vibrant, guitar-driven performances. Known for their exceptional musicianship and deep appreciation of the Dead’s catalog, the group delivers faithful interpretations while embracing the spontaneity and exploration that define jam-band culture. Their concerts feature intricate harmonies, extended instrumental passages, and a relaxed yet energetic atmosphere that appeals to both longtime Deadheads and newer audiences. By combining technical skill with a genuine love for the music, Grateful Shred creates an engaging live experience that honors the enduring legacy of the Grateful Dead.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.title: Turning Night! Guided Open Studio with Matt Iannacci
events.description: Open to anyone who's tried their hand at woodturning, come spend the evening making your latest project under Matt's guidance! 3-Hour Guided Open Studio Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Time: 6–9pm Description: Spend the evening on the lathes with fellow turners! Join us for Turning Night, a guided open studio session open to anyone who’s taken a woodturning workshop with us before—or anyone with experience on a wood lathe at all! Come with a project idea and Matt will guide you through the setup and technique to make it happen. This is the perfect opportunity for anyone with some turning experience to pursue their own project—but in the presence of an experienced woodturning instructor! The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, including pen blanks ( pen kit available here ), spindle blanks, and bowl blanks. However, for a more specific project, students are welcome to bring a wood blank of their own (we recommend Rockler if purchasing in advance). Join us for a night of woodturning community, guidance, and fun! Thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop and Matt Iannacci for his expertise and enthusiasm! Tuition: $45 Materials: The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, or students can BYOB (blank)! Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist: Matt Iannacci “I have been woodturning for over 10 years, and doing wood flatwork for more than 7 years. I focus on medium-sized peices (vases, urns, etc., in woodturning, and jewelry boxes and frames in flatwork), usually seeking to combine different wood species to provide color and texture in my pieces. I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: Judy Collins
events.description: Judy Collins is a legendary folk singer-songwriter known for her crystal-clear vocals, poetic songwriting, and influential role in the American folk music revival of the 1960s. Her music blends folk, pop, and traditional ballad influences while often exploring themes of love, social awareness, introspection, and human connection. Collins became widely respected for interpreting songs by iconic songwriters and for helping introduce audiences to many influential artists throughout her long career. With decades of acclaimed performances, timeless recordings, and a graceful stage presence, Judy Collins remains one of the most celebrated voices in folk and contemporary acoustic music.

events.title: Needle Felting: Bird of the Month: Chickadee with Erin Carlson
events.description: November’s bird of the month: Chickadee! Learn to needle felt, while enjoying a detailed look at this fascinating bird! 3-hour workshop Date: Thursday, November 5 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: Learn to needle felt or sharpen your skills while creating your own Chickadee . Fiber artist and backyard bird enthusiast Erin Carlson of Red Cottage Fiber Studio will guide you through the needle felting process as you look closely to observe the shape and markings of the species and gain a deeper appreciation of our avian neighbors. Adventurous beginners welcome. Please note that we will be using sharp needles and repetitive, detailed hand motions. About the 2026-27 Bird of the Month Needle Felting Series : Due to popular demand, Contemporary Craft is thrilled to once again partner with instructor Erin Carlson to offer this series of workshops! While first offered virtually during the pandemic, this year will be live and in-person! Classes will occur the first Thursday of each month from 6-9pm and run from March 2026-February 2027. Join us for as many classes as you like. Choose your favorite bird or join us for all 12 to complete your very own flock. The bird selections are as follows: March: American Robin April: Scarlet Tanager May: Barn Swallow June: Eastern Bluebird July: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird August: American Goldfinch September: Downy Woodpecker October: Barn Owl November: Chickadee December: Northern Cardinal January(2027): Red Breasted Nuthatch February(2027): Red Winged Blackbird Tuition: $65 + $10 materials fee (per workshop) (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Erin Carlson is a multidiscplinary fiber artist working and teaching in th Pittsburgh area for the last decade. She loves to help students explore their creativity through the use of fibers.

events.title: Matilda - The Musical
events.description: Matilda – The Musical is a Tony Award-winning and Olivier Award-winning stage production that brings Roald Dahl's beloved story to life through imaginative storytelling, unforgettable songs, and spectacular choreography. Featuring a clever score by Tim Minchin and a book by Dennis Kelly, the musical follows the brilliant and determined young Matilda Wormwood as she discovers the power of courage, friendship, and imagination while standing up to injustice. Packed with witty humor, larger-than-life characters, and visually inventive staging, the production balances heartfelt emotion with high-energy musical numbers that appeal to audiences of all ages. From the unforgettable Miss Trunchbull to the kindhearted Miss Honey, each character contributes to a story that celebrates intelligence, resilience, and the belief that even the smallest voice can make a profound difference. With its award-winning music, inspiring message, and extraordinary theatrical creativity, Matilda – The Musical continues to delight theatergoers around the world as one of the most acclaimed family musicals of the modern era.

events.title: Andi Gladwin in Shuffled
events.description: Andi Gladwin's new intimate magic show unveils a mesmerizing fusion of storytelling, technology, and your very own deck of cards! An electrifying evening of magic awaits you for this brand-new show, developed exclusively for performances at Liberty Magic.Each guest is invited to bring their own deck of cards. A deck kept from Grandmother’s Bridge game? A tourist deck from your last vacation? The family Uno deck? Whatever the deck, bring it along, and it will become part of the show in the hands of a master of sleight-of-hand.British magician Andi Gladwin has dedicated his life to magic as co-founder of Vanishing Inc., one of the world’s largest magic brands, and as an in-demand performer. He has performed all over the world at prestigious events such as in Washington, DC for President Obama’s Inauguration, the world's most expensive private yacht, and more.“The best magic creates a story,” Andi says. “My aim is for everyone to walk away with a new experience that they will talk about for the rest of their lives.” Those stories have been told by guests at thousands of events over the past decade.Andi was a winner of Penn & Teller: Fool Us, where he managed to leave the magic duo completely dumfounded. He has also appeared on British ITV's Next Great Magician and is a season regular on CW Channel's Masters of Illusion. His magic is funny, upbeat, and downright deceiving. You’ll be talking about it for years to come, and you’ll never look at that family deck of cards in the same way again.“I can confidently say that ‘Shuffled’ is one of the best close-up magic shows I have ever witnessed.” — Suburban Chicagoland

events.title: Jesse Cook
events.description: Jesse Cook is an acclaimed Canadian guitarist, composer, and producer celebrated for his distinctive blend of nuevo flamenco, rumba, jazz, world music, and contemporary instrumental sounds. His performances showcase expressive nylon-string guitar work, intricate rhythms, and a richly atmospheric style shaped by musical influences from Spain, Latin America, the Middle East, and beyond. Cook’s extensive catalog includes fan favorites such as *Tempest*, *Gravity*, *The Rumba Foundation*, and *Beyond Borders*. His latest album, *past the breakwater*, is scheduled for release on September 18, 2026, offering a timely introduction to the evolving artistry of this internationally recognized musician.

events.title: Colby T. Helms
events.description: DOORS 7PM | SHOW 8PM$18 ADV | $23Every town has them. The underdogs. The people who never quite fit in. The ones who are misunderstood. The ones who strive, stumble, and keep going anyway.With his second album, One for the Losers, Colby T. Helms tells their stories.Raised in the Blue Ridge foothills of Southwest Virginia, Helms launched his career as a teenager, writing raw and ragged songs that drew from the people, places, stories, and struggles that shaped him. If his debut album chronicled his own experience, then One for the Losers widens the frame by looking outward. Across a dozen tracks, Helms shines a light on the overlooked and misunderstood characters whove crossed his path, from troubled friends and fallen mentors to moonshiners, immigrants, and working-class Virginians trying to survive in a world that threatens to leave them behind.

events.title: SOPHIE BUDDLE (Thursday)
events.description: Sophie Buddle is a stand-up, a TV writer, and a podcaster. She has just wrapped as the head monologue writer for “After Midnight with Taylor Tomlinson.” She has also appeared on “The Tonight Show”, “The Late Late Show with James Corden”, and on CBC’s “This Hour Has 22 Minutes as a correspondent and staff writer. She's also been featured on CTV’s "Roast Battle", JFL All Access, Kevin Hart's LOL Network, the Winnipeg Comedy Festival and the Halifax Comedy Festival. She was a featured performer at the Just For Laughs Comedy Festival in Montreal and in 2022 had the esteemed privilege of delivering the Canadian Keynote Address on Comedy. Why'd We Book It? Sophie is witty, self-depricating, and extremely candid. We were so excited to hear about her podcast, "Obsessed with Sophie Buddle", which has some of our favorite comics on as guests. Her and her guests will talk about her latest obsessions like smoking, Tiktok, and Nintendo switch - which we can all relate to. Her style stood out to us when she did The Late Late show with a joke about being cheated on, but don't worry she doesn't own a baseball bat. For Fans Of... Taylor Tomlinson, Iliza Schlesinger, Nicole Byer Extended Bio: Sophie released her first album in 2019, "Lil Bit Of Buddle," which won the 2020 Juno Award for Best Comedy Album of the Year, making her the first female comic to win that award. She released the album herself so you can find it on iTunes in the genre "easy listening", which was a mistake, but it is easy to listen to, so it's OK. Her podcast "Obsessed with Sophie Buddle", which tackles people’s obsessions (from Beyoncé to American politics to checking if the door is locked to revenge) is currently available on Apple Podcasts. She is a three-time runner up (but fourth time’s the charm!) for Canada's biggest stand-up contest, SiriusXM Top Comic, and can currently be seen headlining across the country. events.title: “Road to Revolution” Seminar at Fort Ligonier
events.description: Join us for an extraordinary two-day "Road to Revolution" Seminar featuring a distinguished panel of speakers who will discuss Revolutionary moments in history to celebrate America's 250th anniversary!For America’s Semiquincentenial anniversary, Fort Ligonier is partnering with Emerging Revolutionary War Era to bring you all the REVOLUTIONARY information you desire! Learn about the crucial ties that connect the French and Indian War to the War for American Independence with Revolutionary topics!2026 Seminar Speakers: Michael C. HarrisMichael C. Harris is a graduate of the University of Mary Washington and American Military University. He has worked with the National Park Service in Fredericksburg, Virginia; Fort Mott State Park in New Jersey; and the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission at Brandywine Battlefield. Mike has led tours and staff rides at numerous East Coast battlefields. His first book, Brandywine, received the American Revolution Round Table of Richmond Book Award in 2014.Daniel WelchDan Welch has served as editor of Gettysburg Magazine, a National Park Service ranger at Gettysburg National Military Park, and Education Programs Coordinator for the Gettysburg Foundation. He co-authored two books in the Emerging Civil War Series: The Last Road North: A Guide to the Gettysburg Campaign, 1863 and Never Such a Campaign: The Battle of Second Manassas, August 28–30, 1862. His latest work, Conquer or Die: The 1776 New York Campaign, explores the important but often overlooked battles for New York during the Revolution’s pivotal year.Greg Urwin, Ph.D.Gregory J.W. Urwin is a professor of history at Temple University, a prize-winning author, and a former president of the Society for Military History. He recently retired as general editor of the Campaigns and Commanders book series at University of Oklahoma Press, which he helmed since 1999. A specialist in U.S. and British military history, Urwin earned his PhD at the University of Notre Dame. During Professor Urwin’s decades of teaching, he trained twenty-six Ph.D.’s in military history.Urwin is an award-winning author whose work has been recognized by the Marine Corps Historical Foundation, the Little Big Horn Associates, and the Eastern National Park and Monument Association. He has written nine books, including his latest, When Freedom Wore a Red Coat: The British, the Enslaved, and the War in the South, 1780-81. He has also appeared in numerous documentaries, including programs on the History Channel and Pennsylvania Cable Network.Kevin J. Weddle, Ph.D.Kevin Weddle is a Distinguished Fellow and a military historian at the US Army War College in Carlisle, Pennsylvania. He is a graduate of the US Military Academy, a combat veteran, and served over 28 years on active duty in the US Army before retiring as a colonel. He is a multiple award-winning author of books and articles, including the critically acclaimed and best-selling The Compleat Victory: Saratoga and the American Revolution (Oxford University Press, 2021), winner of six national and international literary awards including the Gilder Lehrman Prize in Military History and the Society of the Cincinnati Prize. He leads military and civilian groups to battlefields around the world and specializes in the American Revolution, the American Civil War, the Second World War, general military history, and military technology.James M. Vaughn, Ph.D. “The Great War for Empire and the Origins of the American Revolution: A Revisionist Account.”James M. Vaughn is a historian of the global British Empire and the Atlantic world during the eighteenth century. He teaches at the University of Chicago, where he serves as an Associate Instructional Professor in the College and an Affiliate Faculty Member in the Department of History. He is the author of The Politics of Empire at the Accession of George III: The East India Company and the Crisis and Transformation of Britain’s Imperial State (Yale University Press), the co-editor of Envisioning Empire: The New British World from 1763 to 1773 (Bloomsbury) and Capitalism: Histories (Boydell & Brewer) and is currently writing a book on the origins of the American Revolution.About the “Road to Revolution” Seminar and the Braddock Road Preservation AssociationThe “Road to Revolution” Seminar honors the legacy of the Braddock Road Preservation Association.The Braddock Road Preservation Association was formed in 1989 as the Jumonville Preservation Association. It was formed to research, develop, interpret and promote the French and Indian War history of Jumonville, Dunbar’s Camp, and the Braddock Road. In 2025, the organization was dissolved after 36 years, but their seminar continues at Fort Ligonier.Fort Ligonier is partnering this year with the Emerging Revolutionary War (ERW) ERW, which serves as a public history-oriented platform dedicated to sharing original scholarship and discussion on the American Revolution. The ERW encourages our citizens to learn about our nation’s founding at the original places where the historic events occurred via their blog, podcasts, tours, and on-site videos.

events.title: Kamasi Washington
events.description: Kamasi Washington is an acclaimed saxophonist, composer and bandleader whose expansive sound blends contemporary jazz with elements of funk, gospel, classical music and hip-hop. Known for his powerful live ensembles and adventurous arrangements, he first gained broad attention through his landmark album The Epic and collaborations with artists including Kendrick Lamar. His fifth studio album, Fearless Movement, explores rhythm, dance and the emotional connections between generations. Washington’s performances offer an immersive jazz experience shaped by soaring saxophone lines, dynamic instrumentation and a spirit of musical discovery.
