events.title: Basketry: Gifting Goodies Basket with Traycee Bosle
events.description: Enjoy two peaceful Saturday afternoons with Traycee, and create a charming basket perfect for gifting homemade goodies this season! Basketry: Gifting Goodies Basket with Traycee Bosle two day workshop Date: Saturdays December 5 and 12 Time: 2PM – 5PM Description: Enjoy two peaceful Saturday afternoons learning with the luminous Traycee Bosle, whose love of basketry is a pure joy to be around. And, create a sweet and giftable basket while you do! In this two-day workshop students will create a charming 12″ x 6″ x 6″ rectangular basket inspired by traditional Colonial-style basketry. Students will learn plaiting techniques using narrow rows, construct a sturdy rectangular form, and work with a notched handle. A distinctive wooden “ribbon” accent in festive holiday colors adds a special decorative touch. The finished basket is perfect for filling with homemade goodies to give as a thoughtful handmade gift—or to enjoy as seasonal décor in your own home. Tuition: $130 + $18 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. Registration: Register through Eventbrite, if you are viewing this listing via the CC website on your mobile device, click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are often available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Find more information and find the scholarship application here. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Paper Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hall from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything that would be helpful for us to know before you arrive, please leave a message for Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or by email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Traycee Bosle is a professional basket weaver at Craftisinal Creative Works—her arts studio in Pittsburgh, PA. She is a member of the Handweavers Guild of America and the Fiber Arts Guild of Pittsburgh. With over 1500 works in several different weaving styles under her belt, you can find her work in homes across the U.S. Basketweaving is an ancient art that crosses nearly all time, geographic, political, and social boundaries. It’s rooted in history, mathematics and pattern, color theory and design—with so much to offer—yet it’s nearly a lost art. Traycee has made it her mission to share her love for this once ubiquitous and critical skill with people of all ages. Her classes are fun, informative and personalized! She provides hands-on, individualized instruction using her own specially designed basket kits to teach the fundamentals of the art and meet each student where they are in their skill level. Whether you are an absolute beginner or have already made a few baskets, you will walk away with new skills and a beautiful basket you can use every day.

events.description: 🎄 Claus for a Cause: A Holiday Celebration for Every Family 🎅Join us for the 2nd Annual Claus for a Cause, a festive holiday celebration created by local families affected by Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) and open to everyone!Prader-Willi syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects hunger regulation, metabolism, muscle tone, and more. For families living with PWS, the holidays can bring unique challenges, especially when food is at the center of so many traditions. Claus for a Cause was created to offer a joyful, inclusive space where families can celebrate the season, make memories, and simply enjoy being together.✨ Your ticket includes:🎅 Photos with Santa🍽️ A family-friendly lunch🎁 Silent auction🎨 Kids crafts and festive activities🐾 Therapy pup visits🎈 Face painting🎄 And plenty of holiday cheer!The event is a fundraiser benefiting PWSA | USA, helping provide advocacy, family support, education, and research for individuals and families affected by Prader-Willi syndrome.Come celebrate the season, support a meaningful cause, and help us create a holiday experience where every family feels welcome. ❤️The venue is ADA compliant; wheelchair and stroller friendly. Event offerings subject to change.

events.title: Gwar with Midnight, Mac Sabbath and X-Cops
events.description: GWAR is a legendary heavy metal band known for outrageous theatrical performances, elaborate sci-fi costumes, and shock-rock stage shows filled with satire, horror, and over-the-top spectacle. Their music blends thrash metal, punk, hardcore, and heavy metal influences with dark humor, aggressive riffs, and chaotic live energy. GWAR concerts are famous for immersive visual effects, fictional storylines, and outrageous audience interaction that have made the band one of the most unique acts in heavy music history. With decades of cult popularity and an uncompromising artistic identity, GWAR remains an iconic force in theatrical metal entertainment.Midnight is a blackened speed metal band recognized for raw aggression, fast-paced riffs, and a gritty sound inspired by classic heavy metal, punk, and extreme underground music. Their music combines high-speed intensity, snarling vocals, and old-school metal attitude into relentless songs driven by chaos and rebellion. Midnight has earned a loyal following through energetic live performances and a stripped-down approach that captures the spirit of vintage extreme metal.Mac Sabbath is a parody metal band known for combining fast-food satire with Black Sabbath-inspired heavy metal music and theatrical comedy performances. Dressed in exaggerated fast-food-themed costumes, the group delivers humorous reimagined versions of classic metal songs while creating a bizarre and highly entertaining stage production. Their concerts blend comedy, heavy riffs, and absurd visual storytelling into a unique live experience that has gained cult popularity among metal and comedy fans alike.X-Cops is a hardcore and thrash crossover band built around a satirical law-enforcement theme, featuring aggressive metal riffs, humorous storytelling, and over-the-top stage personas. Known for blending heavy music with comedic performance elements, the group delivers chaotic live shows driven by punk energy and theatrical intensity. Their music combines hardcore aggression with tongue-in-cheek humor that appeals strongly to fans of underground metal and parody-driven performance art.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

Their performances showcase remarkable vocal precision, clever mashups, and engaging choreography, creating a concert experience that is equal parts musical excellence and lighthearted entertainment. Whether performing festive holiday favorites or imaginative reinterpretations of well-known songs, Straight No Chaser consistently captivates audiences with its polished musicianship, charismatic stage presence, and effortless chemistry. With multiple chart-topping albums, extensive international touring, and a reputation for delivering unforgettable live shows, Straight No Chaser continues to redefine what is possible in contemporary a cappella music.

events.title: WILD PINK
events.description: WILD PINK with support from HIDING PLACES $20 ADV / $25 DOS 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES for fans of... This is Lorelei, Ratboys, MJ Lenderman, Waxahatchee BIO: There’s a novelistic impression to the songs of Wild Pink, where characters peer over the edge of potential futures, past mistakes and paths not taken. Backed by a dive bar hue, NYC-based frontman John Ross blends the existential with the celestial, gathering pieces of passer-bys, fictional figures, and historical idiosyncrasies to make sense of what’s in front of him. It’s on their sixth album, Still Coming Down, that Ross cements the voice he’s been steadily honing over the years. The album pokes fun at the listlessness of consumerism, coping through detachment and finding the punchline of it all. Ross is a consummate of curiosity, becoming a narrator of a warped and unpredictable America, morphing everyday mundanity into a cinematic, sepia-toned flipbook. Propelled by the witty and ravenous wisdom of 2024’s Dulling the Horns, Ross’ poetic form has only gained traction, as jocular, heartfelt stories pour with a clever and distinctive ease. NFL bros cruise alongside big guys in grocery stores with even bigger tattoos; ghost stories and references from the cinematic haze of movies like Heat, Moneyball and The Town buzz in the background while Ross also points to Waterworld and The Perfect Storm––heroes who wander, looking for answers at the end of the world. After battling––and beating––cancer, and now becoming a father for the first time, Ross’ outlook has hairpin-bent its way into a simpler significance, where creating music is less about the bigger picture, and more about being present in the moment. It’s a genuine rock record, leaning into the dynamics of open-armed arrangements, inviting huge chords, harmonicas, horns, keys and pedal steel to morph and blend into a cathartic swirl. Ross looked back to the grunge bands he was obsessed with as a teen, and found that it sparked a deeper presence with his own voice, both in lyrics and performance. He endeavoured to create an album that is as fun to play live as it is for the audience to witness, harkening back to the enthusiasm and motivation he felt growing up. “Strangely, I feel like I've found my voice on this record,” he says. Still Coming Down was recorded in one week in Asheville, NC at the renowned Drop of Sun studios with producer and engineer Alex Farrar (Bnny, Wednesday, Samia). Vocal takes were done in two to three bursts, marking a less laborious process than previous records. “There was not a ton of overthinking,” Ross says. He invited friends to collaborate throughout, mimicking the carousel of characters that comes with living a life on the road. Longtime Wild Pink member Dan Keegan lends his percussive talents, with Meg Duffy (Hand Habits), MJ Lenderman and Lenderman’s The Wind bandmates Landon George and Xandy Chelmis adding a raucous vigor to the arrangements. On opener “Box Store” Ross is that college buddy lamenting the empty desires of folks strolling the strip mall and the irony of AC units blocking the view during one of the year’s best seasons. Hearty keys and groaning steel are teamed with electric plucks, piecing together a bursting introduction. “500 is in the New 250” bounces between scuzzy guitars and softer, reflective moments, portraying the push-and-pull of cacophonous rock clubs and the long, quiet drive to the next hotel, bandmates silently staring into their phones. The sauntering “Still Coming Down” captures Ross’ ability to pinpoint some of the more painful parts of life with an eye on a more hopeful horizon. All’s not lost despite the darkness, as Ross relays “I used to be pure / I just try to be good now,” over Duffy’s guitar and George’s fiddle. “Round of Applause At The End Of The World” points to the whirlpools of conspiracy theories and the cloud of misinformation that can take over entire communities. “I don’t know what my idea of fun is anymore,” Ross calls, wry and weary, as distorted guitars respond resolute. The song ends abruptly, like a person you can’t convince otherwise. Still Coming Down is a storied expedition that welcomes in the drifters and the kids kicking up dust; the brokenhearted and the cursed; the ones looking for an answer and the ones who simply couldn’t care less. Ross gives movement to the characters in our heads, the faces we see every few years and the ones who pass us by. It’s proper rock meant to be played loud, with your hand out the car window, riding the air as you bound down some highway in the early hours. Forming soon-to-be-classics that soak in their ability to impact without unnecessary frills, Still Coming Down is about the very nature of songwriting and instinct, learning to trust the process and staying open to the lessons you might learn along the way.

events.title: KING TUFF + SHEER MAG
events.description: KING TUFF + SHEER MAG with support tba $25 ADV / $28 DOS 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES for fans of... Ty Segall, Shannon and the Clams, Screaming Females KING TUFF BIO: There are times in our life when we feel magic in the air. When new love arrives, or we find ourselves lost in a moment of creation with others who share our vision. A sense that: this is who I want to be. This is what I want to share. It’s a fleeting feeling and one that Kyle Thomas, the singer-songwriter who records and performs as King Tuff, found himself longing for in the spring of 2020. But knowing he couldn’t simply recreate this time in his life at will, Thomas—who hails from Brattleboro, Vermont—set out to write a love letter to those cherished moments of inspiration and to the small town that formed him. The one where he first nurtured his songwriting impulses, bouncing ideas off other like-minded artists. The kind of place where the changing of the seasons always delivered a sense of perspective and fresh artistic inspiration. Where he felt a deeper connection with nature and sense of community that had once been so close at hand. “I wanted to make an album to remind myself that life is magical,” he reflects. And so, Thomas seized upon his memories, creating what he calls “an album about love and nature and youth.” The result is Smalltown Stardust, a spiritual, tender and ultimately joyous record that might come as a shock to those with only a passing knowledge of the artist’s back catalog. On Smalltown Stardust, Thomas takes us on his journey to a place where past and present collide, where he can be a dreamer in love with all that he sees. Images of his youth abound: from Route 91 which runs through his hometown (in “Smalltown Stardust”); to Redtooth, a spectre who used to roam the streets (“Bandits Of Blue Sky”); to old friends, old haunts and old dreams (“Always Find Me”); to Vermont’s Rock River, which gave its name to a song of a torch still burning for past love: “Those days are gone and we can’t rewind/ Cuz people grow and places change/ But my love for you will never fade away.” But at the core of Smalltown Stardust is Thomas’s desire to commune with nature on a spiritual level. Images of the natural world, from blizzards to green mountains to cloudy days, fill the songs and create a setting unmistakably far away from Los Angeles. “I consider nature to be my religion,” he explains, and Smalltown Stardust is nothing if not a spiritual exploration. Thomas’s identification as a sort of eternal spiritual seeker is underscored in one of the album’s sweetest moments, “A Meditation,” which features a home audio recording of Thomas as an eight year old, trying his hand at leading a meditation. It’s a journey that he continues to this day, as he intones on “Portrait of God”: “Walking in the woods, wading in the river” and “breathing in the mountain air” before heading back to a place where he finds himself “Oil painting in my garage/Let my colors flow/ I’m working on my portrait of God.” While so much of Smalltown Stardust invokes idealized traces and places of Thomas’s past, the album’s recording process made his communal vision a reality. Thomas’s Los Angeles home in2020formed a micro-scene of sorts, with housemates Meg Duffy (Hand Habits) and Sasami Ashworth recording their own heralded albums (2021’s Fun House and 2022’s Squeeze, respectively) at the same time. A shared spirit dominated an era spent largely on the premises, with Thomas serving as engineer and contributor to both records, and Ashworth working as co-producer on Smalltown Stardust. Thomas describes the time with a fitting metaphor: “I’ve always thrived around other people making things. You want to bloom with each other.”Ashworth’s contributions are vital to the album: she co-wrote a majority of the record and contributed vocals, arrangements, and instrumentation to each song. As Thomas notes, “I tried to follow her vision a lot. It helps to open your world to collaborators. You always get something completely different than you would have expected.” With the gorgeous orchestral tones of “Love Letter to Plants,” it’s immediately clear that Thomas is declaring a wider vision of what his music can be. Gone are many of the squalling guitars of previous King Tuff records, replaced with thoughtful, tender touches of cello and violin on “LoveLetter to Plants,” “Pebbles In A Stream” and “The Bandits Of Blue Sky”; a plaintive saxophoneon “Always Find Me”; and orchestral vocal harmonies with Ashworth that lift the songs to acelestial plane. (Though the rollicking, joyous leads on “Portrait of God” show Thomas hasn’t lost his touch on guitar.) On “How I Love,” Thomas makes clear that all of this is by design: “So lost in nothing but noise for so many years, I forgot to love.” In the end, Smalltown Stardust is not merely a nostalgia trip. In making the record, Thomas not only conjured a special time in his life, he found new inspiration, surrounded by a small circle of collaborators and a sense of love and wonder for nature. If the first King Tuff record was content to merely state Thomas was no longer dead, Smalltown Stardust is a paean to what that life means. A statement of belief and a hymnal to the magic still to behold all around us. “I’m a different person now than I was 20 years ago when I first started it. But oddly, when I first started the band, it was more like this,” he says. Which is to say, things have come full circle. Or as Thomas intones on “The Wheel”: “Ooh we were just kids then… Caught up in the turning of the wheel…. And it’s coming ‘round again.” SHEER MAG BIO: Underlying every great record, every career-defining work of art, is a certain ineffable, increasingly rarified quality: unity of vision. Great songs need not announce their greatness: their marriage of idea with action, soul with sound, appears as something which is naturally effortless, unforced—they are what they are because they have no choice but to be. On Playing Favorites, Sheer Mag’s third full length and first with Third Man Records, this precise, matured clarity of vision is put on full display. Over the course of the past decade, Sheer Mag have labored to carve out a discernibly singular position within the canon of contemporary rock: toggling with ease between the refined flourishes of a “connoisseur’s band” and the ecstatic colloquialism of populist songwriting—yet displaying no strict loyalty to either camp—their sound, while oft-referenced, is unmistakably and immediately recognizable as theirs alone. With Playing Favorites, Sheer Mag have capitalized on a decade’s worth of devotion to their own collective spirit—a spirit refined in both the sweaty trenches of punk warehouses and the larger-than-life glamour of concert halls—emerging with a dense work of gripping emotions, massive hooks, and masterfully constructed power-pop anthems. This is the record the Philadelphian rock and roll four-piece has always been destined to make. Playing Favorites expands with a sense of undeniable vitality, buoyed by rock and roll’s singular capacity to channel a relentless compassion for human life. While at times marked by an intensified sense of melancholy, this newest offering takes stock of the confusing flow of daily life without moralizing, refusing to fall into antagonistic cynicism. Sheer Mag leans into the chaotic thrall of city living, of a life subdivided by the jagged highs and lows of bars, parties, and nightlife culture, with sweetly empathetic remove. The chemically-saturated swing of disco rhythms, crooning earnestness of heartland Americana, and boisterous theatrics of capital-G-and-M Guitar Music become strangely familiar bedfellows. This music is complex, not complicated. As lead guitarist Kyle Seely puts it, “I don’t believe people should put on a record and have to work to enjoy it.” Sheer Mag neither pander towards the studied pretensions of the rock historian elite nor dilute their approach into something more blankly palatable to a commercial audience. Instead, they have their eyes set on that ever elusive third option: those who just get it. If you build it, they will come. Sheer Mag began to work in earnest on their follow up to 2019’s A Distant Call in the summer of 2021, which they originally imagined would take the shape of a tautly constructed 4-song disco EP. As Matt Palmer, the band’s rhythm guitarist and primary lyricist, recollects: “those first four songs came out of a hard moment in life for all of us collectively—they kind of felt like an attempt to figure out how to have fun when you actually feel miserable.” Before long, the band realized this new material would perhaps be better served within the context of a fully fleshed out rock LP, bracketed by the support of a wider array of juxtaposing psychic moods and sonic textures. Over a six-month stretch spanning the fall of 2022 to the winter of 2023, Kyle Seely and his brother Hart Seely (bass) set about tracking the instrumentals for the record, resetting their studio configuration each week in order to impose a more tailored, multi-session atmosphere upon the record’s acoustic landscape. Palmer rejoined vocalist Tina Halladay in Philadelphia the following spring to write and record the vocals for Playing Favorites, which depart rather markedly from the band’s prior material, placing an added emphasis on pronouncedly existential, interpersonal storytelling and ornate background harmonies. Reflecting upon the shift between this newest LP and the band’s previous material, Halladay notes: “those first few records felt like a personal coming out party; they felt like they were an introduction to me and my life story. With these new songs, I feel like I’m finally able to move past that—there are parts on this record that I couldn’t imagine being able to sing ten, five, or even three years ago.” Playing Favorites burns with a sweetened gratitude for the lot one has been given in life: the luck of coming up punk; the luck of living an unalienated life; the luck of feeling love, and losing love. The title track announces itself with a sense of self-assured swagger, spinning a jubilant tale of life on the road: the band is back together, and they know they’ve never sounded quite this good before. A clamoring gust of socially lubricated bravado weaves its way throughout much of the record, such as on “All Lined Up,” which paints images of late nights (early mornings?) spent amongst possible friends, cigarettes fizzing in the ashtrays and a sense of looming dread curling through the air. Every coin has two sides, of course: the candor of Playing Favorites’ sweeter moments is often balanced by a certain studied sadness, that soft grief of living that negatively lends such brighter moments their seductive allure. “Golden Hour” conjures a softly elegiac longing, evoking images of old photographs which shimmer like the fields of Elysium; “When You Get Back” croons about fantasies of a loving future which may never come. Sheer Mag have broken significant musical ground with Playing Favorites, elevating their signature approach to rock and roll to lushly cinematic new heights. “Moonstruck,” for instance, lives up to its titular reference of Hollywood-sized surprise romance, spooling out a charming story of desire crossing the liquid boundary that separates innocent crush from deepening love. Playing Favorites’ filmic qualities reach their peak on “Mechanical Garden,” which lurches forth like a three-part fugue, carrying the listener from ripping glam theatrics into a subtly psychedelic, string and drum machine dub interlude, finally resolving upon perhaps the most openly depressive iteration of Sheer Mag’s take on disco-inflected pop, outfitted with a guest guitar solo by Mdou Moctar. The baroque elegance of such moments find their natural counterpoint in the record’s more straightforward power-pop tracks, such as “Don’t Come Looking,” which courses with the chest-filling bravado of a lightly southern-fried Nerves hit, and “Paper Time,” which delivers a type of mad-dash snare-roll catharsis that brings to mind all of the giddy melodrama of the final heist in a Cassavetes movie. Playing Favorites’ greatest achievement, however, is perhaps its unabashed embrace of nakedly emotional, arena-sized choruses, which seem to fizz out of some sort of timeless radio set to the frequency of pure human experience. As Halladay puts it, “Nobody seems to write straight up rock bangers anymore–more than anything else, we want this record to put huge, catchy songwriting front and center.” Playing Favorites is undoubtedly a record by the same Sheer Mag that audiences of all stripes have spent the last decade falling in love with. In fact, for all of its sonic departures and evolutions, this record is perhaps the most “Sheer Mag” release yet. Not so much a return to form, but rather a realization of those greatest promises that the band has up until now only hinted at. With Playing Favorites, Sheer Mag cater to their tastes and their tastes alone: so long as they continue to do so, the future of rock and roll, that great human tradition, is in the best of hands.

events.title: Kyle Gordon
events.description: Kyle Gordon is a comedian, musician, writer, and digital creator who has built a large online following through his clever character work, satirical songs, and sharp observations about internet culture and everyday life. His comedy often parodies specific musical styles, nostalgic pop-culture trends, and exaggerated personalities, combining polished production with intentionally over-the-top performances that have become widely shared across social media platforms. In addition to creating viral comedy videos, Gordon has expanded his career into live performances where he blends stand-up, original music, and theatrical storytelling into an interactive entertainment experience. His ability to faithfully recreate the sounds and aesthetics of different musical eras while adding humorous twists has earned praise from audiences who appreciate both the craftsmanship and the comedy behind his work. As his fan base continues to grow, Kyle Gordon has established himself as one of the most inventive comedic performers of the digital era, seamlessly bridging online entertainment and live stage performance.

events.title: Weave Your Own Towel with the CC Weave Coaches: Holiday Special!
events.description: Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! Drop on in and weave a towel! We did the set up for you! Yes, absolute beginners welcome! DROP IN STYLE: 3-hour session! Date: Saturday, December 12! Time: Start times vary: 10 AM, 12PM, 2PM (and expect to stay for about 3 hours after your start time for your towel to reach completion!). You will select your start time when you register. Description: Weaving Curious? This is your chance!!! Absolute beginner drop-in style weaving has arrived! Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! You, too, can make your very own towel! Come on in and weave on pre-dressed looms! Our team of Weave Coaches will prepare your looms before you get here! All, you will need to do is choose some yarn colors and throw a shuttle. And…..not to worry! our Weave Coaches will guide you through the process, offering tips for throwing those shuttles back and forth to build a special and custom towel of your very own design. What’s more, we will help you take the weaving off of the loom and finish and hem your towel before you leave the studio! You can expect your towel to be about 16 x 20 inches (and it will shrink after washing to about 14 x 18), so as a dear weaver once said these will be “towel-ish” sized, and all a bit different. A sweet hand towel to gift to a loved one or to brighten up your own room! This is a completely beginners welcome offering. No experience expected. There are different beginning time slots to choose. Plan to spend about 3 hours from your chosen start time. For this special holiday edition: Five weavers will be able to begin at each starting time; call up all of your best pals and have a SUPER FUN time together! This is offering is part of our Gift Guide suite of workshops, in which you get to learn something and make a gift for someone special at the same time! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please visit this link which will take you to the Eventbrite listing. events.title: Woodworking 101 with David Bielewicz
events.description: Learn the basics of wood shop machines, processes, and safety in this introductory course! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Wednesday, December 16, 2026 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: This designed-for-beginners course will explore the basics of woodworking in a judgement-free environment! Using the core machines of the wood studio, students will learn the lumber milling process—turning a rough-sawn board into dimensional lumber—which is the launching pad for nearly every wood project. Folks will build familiarity with the studio space, tools, and safety considerations and will walk away with several sample pieces demonstrating knowledge and confidence in the woodshop. If you’re hesitant to jump into one of our project-based workshops or curious if woodworking is even right for you, this is a great place to start! events.title: Magnolia Boulevard w/ Madison Hughes
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$15 ADV | $20 DOS21+With a southern rock tinged flavor of soulful americana, and a powerful female vocalist reminiscent of Tedeschi Trucks Band, Magnolia Boulevard has blossomed through devastation since forming in 2017. They pushed through the turmoil of COVID-19 that devastated the music industry, the sorrow following the death of their beloved drummer, and the joys of welcoming Maggies daughter into the world. Much like the band members of Magnolia Boulevard have endured the highs and lows of the past few years, so has their music. The bands emphatic and empowering anthems of love, self-discovery, grief, and uncertainty serve as a lesson to us all about lifes unpredictable nature and how to better live in the moment so we can appreciate everything and everyone around us before theyre gone.If patience is a virtue, then the current state of Magnolia Boulevard plays right into the long-held notion that sonic grandeur evolves in its own time and place one where the Lexington, Kentucky, rock-n-soul act is aiming to break into a national audience ready and roaring for the quintets soaring talents.Formed in 2017 by Noelle and Allen, the band came together when other creative endeavors werent fulfilling the artistic desires and professional expectations of what the duo were envisioning. It was time to push down the gas pedal on the possibility and potential of what Magnolia Boulevard could be, and ultimately has become in sonic design and in the live realm.The sound has been described as Appalachian Soul, and I really like that because of our Appalachian roots, Noelle says. You get a taste of folk with the songwriting portion, but you also have that rock and soul foundation. Madison Hughes will make you feel like someone finally said the thing out loud. Not loudly. She doesnt need to be. Her voice carries the kind of weight that sneaks up on you, warm and unhurried, until a single line stops you mid-drive and you sit in the parking lot a little longer than you planned.She grew up in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, idyllic by every measure, rooted in the same coastal Southern soil that gave the world Lynyrd Skynyrd, Tom Petty, the Allman Brothers, Tedeschi Trucks Band, and Ray Charles. Music was in the air before it was ever a choice. Her fathers folk-rock records: Springsteen, Jackson Browne, Bonnie Raitt, Sheryl Crow, Gillian Welch. Her mothers soft devastation: Dido, Sarah McLachlan, the Cranberries, Norah Jones. The grit and the tenderness both took root.She started writing songs in high school because heartbreak cracked her open and she couldnt say the hard things any other way. That instinct never left. Her sound refuses to sit still, grunge-folk grit threaded through country soul, blues-pop hooks bleeding into indie Americana, all of it held together by feel rather than formula. In high school she was the girl who sat with everyone at lunch, allergic to the idea that you had to pick a side. Thats still who she is. The genre-crossing isnt a strategy. Its just her nature.

events.description: Trans-Siberian Orchestra is a progressive rock ensemble founded in 1996 by producer and composer Paul O’Neill, known for combining hard rock, classical arrangements, theatrical storytelling, and elaborate synchronized production. The group broke through with its debut album, Christmas Eve and Other Stories, featuring the enduring instrumental “Christmas Eve/Sarajevo 12/24.” TSO also created the holiday rock operas The Christmas Attic and The Lost Christmas Eve, along with the television special The Ghosts of Christmas Eve. Its 2026 winter production marks the group’s 30th anniversary with a reimagined staging of The Ghosts of Christmas Eve and a second set of songs and fan favorites.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.description: City Winery Pittsburgh presents Musiq Soulchild live on December 27th, 28th, and 30th as part of a six show series!Musiq Soulchild returns to Pittsburgh for an extended run of intimate performances at City Winery this December, featuring six shows across three nights. Join us for a special evening of soulful vocals, timeless R&B, and the unmistakable artistry that made Musiq one of the defining voices of his generation.Raised on the sounds of Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, and Donny Hathaway, Musiq Soulchild emerged from Philadelphia’s street music scene to help lead the neo-soul movement into the mainstream. events.title: Dave Matthews Tribute Band
events.description: The Dave Matthews Tribute Band celebrates the music of Dave Matthews Band with a high-energy live performance built around intricate guitar work, soaring violin, smooth saxophone, and exploratory drumming. The Buffalo-based ensemble has been honing its tribute for more than 20 years, with a repertoire spanning classic favorites and later material. Its performances evoke the communal spirit of 1990s tape trading, sing-alongs, and musical discovery while recreating the original band’s distinctive sound. The group’s current Dangerous Hours 2026 NYE Run brings that carefully crafted homage to audiences seeking an immersive jam-rock experience.

events.title: Maybe Happy Ending (Touring)
events.description: Maybe Happy Ending is a tender, original musical romance about Oliver and Claire, two retired Helperbots who find connection, adventure and possibly love in a futuristic Seoul. Blending intimate storytelling, jazz-inflected music and inventive theatrical design, the production explores what it means to be human—even when its central characters are not. Winner of six Tony Awards, including Best Musical, the show is led by Tony Award-winning director Michael Arden, with music and book by Will Aronson and Hue Park. Pittsburgh audiences will experience the production as part of its first North American tour.

events.title: Needle Felting: Bird of the Month: Red Breasted Nuthatch with Erin Carlson
events.description: January (2027)’s bird of the month: Red Breasted Nuthatchl! Learn to needle felt, while enjoying a detailed look at this fascinating bird! 3-hour workshop Date: Thursday, January 7, 2027 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: Learn to needle felt or sharpen your skills while creating your own Red Breasted Nuthatch . Fiber artist and backyard bird enthusiast Erin Carlson of Red Cottage Fiber Studio will guide you through the needle felting process as you look closely to observe the shape and markings of the species and gain a deeper appreciation of our avian neighbors. Adventurous beginners welcome. Please note that we will be using sharp needles and repetitive, detailed hand motions. About the 2026-27 Bird of the Month Needle Felting Series : Due to popular demand, Contemporary Craft is thrilled to once again partner with instructor Erin Carlson to offer this series of workshops! While first offered virtually during the pandemic, this year will be live and in-person! Classes will occur the first Thursday of each month from 6-9pm and run from March 2026-February 2027. Join us for as many classes as you like. Choose your favorite bird or join us for all 12 to complete your very own flock. The bird selections are as follows: March: American Robin April: Scarlet Tanager May: Barn Swallow June: Eastern Bluebird July: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird August: American Goldfinch September: Downy Woodpecker October: Barn Owl November: Chickadee December: Northern Cardinal January(2027): Red Breasted Nuthatch February(2027): Red Winged Blackbird Tuition: $65 + $10 materials fee (per workshop) (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Erin Carlson is a multidiscplinary fiber artist working and teaching in th Pittsburgh area for the last decade. She loves to help students explore their creativity through the use of fibers.

events.title: Weekend 101: Introduction to Weaving on a Floor Loom with Jamie Boyle
events.description: In this weekend beginner workshop, go from a pile of yarn to woven cloth, learn how to use a floor loom, and make new friends! Weeklong Intensive: Introduction to Weaving Date: Saturday January 16 and Sunday January 17, 2027 Time: 10am – 5pm (both days!) Description: Let’s dive deep into weaving for a weekend! This is a 100% beginner weaving workshop, where we will learn to use multi-harness floor looms to create cloth! We will work with 8-harness looms, and explore myriad ways of creating interlacements of warp and weft to create cloth! Because of the “intensive” format of this workshop, we will be able to immerse oursleves completely in the fun and magic of weaving and using a loom. You can expect to learn how to go from having bunch of cones or balls of yarn to woven cloth! We will go through steps and ways to dress the loom (that means get the yarn on the loom) and we will try different techniques for interlacing yarn! Our goal will be a woven sampler of possibilities and a foundation for future weaving work! You will also have access to your loom and open studio for one week after the class to practice what you learned! Tuition: $220 + $30 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided Registration: Register via Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: : We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Jamie Boyle is an artist and weaving teacher who recently moved back to Pittsburgh after living for more than a decade in a studio apartment in Brooklyn, NY with a partner and two cats. They attended public school from grade school through graduate school. Jamie’s first weaving teacher was the artist Ann Hamilton, in whose studio they worked for several years after completing an MFA in sculpture. Subsequently, Owyn Marisol Ruck, Kira Silver, Isa Rodrigues, Kelly Valetta, and Jose Picayo taught Jamie who to use a multi-harness floor loom as a tool for weaving. They have had the great honor of sharing a love of weaving with communities of learners at the Park slope Center for Successful Aging, the National Council of Jewish Women NY Lifetime Learning Center, the Museum of Arts and Design, and the Textile Arts Center, among others. Jamie has participated in artist residencies at the Textile Arts Center (Brooklyn, NY); the Museum of Arts and Design (New York, NY); through the SU-CASA program administered by the Brooklyn Arts Council; and Contemporary Craft (Pittsburgh, PA). Currently, they serve as the Fibers Program Manager at Contemporary Craft.

events.title: The Sound of Music
events.description: The Sound of Music is one of the most beloved and enduring musicals in theater history, captivating audiences with its unforgettable songs, inspiring story, and timeless message of hope, courage, and family. Featuring the iconic score by Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II, the production includes cherished classics such as "Do-Re-Mi," "My Favorite Things," "Edelweiss," "Climb Ev'ry Mountain," and the title song, all of which have become staples of musical theater. Set against the breathtaking backdrop of the Austrian Alps, the story follows Maria, an aspiring nun whose warmth, optimism, and love of music transform the lives of the von Trapp family during a time of great uncertainty. Lavish sets, elegant costumes, memorable choreography, and emotionally resonant performances combine to create an unforgettable theatrical experience that appeals to audiences of all ages. Whether enjoyed for the first time or revisited as a treasured favorite, The Sound of Music continues to enchant theatergoers with its uplifting spirit, extraordinary music, and universal themes of love, resilience, and the power of following one's heart.

events.title: Tommy Emmanuel
events.description: Australian guitarist Tommy Emmanuel is celebrated for virtuosic fingerstyle technique, rhythmic percussion played on the guitar’s body, and a repertoire spanning country, blues, folk, jazz and pop. Chet Atkins named him a Certified Guitar Player, a distinction held by only five musicians. Emmanuel has performed at Carnegie Hall and the Sydney Opera House, collaborated with artists including Mark Knopfler and Joe Walsh, and won a Grammy for Best Instrumental Arrangement for “Folsom Prison Blues.” His notable recordings include The Day Fingerpickers Took Over the World, made with Atkins, and The Mystery.

events.title: A Journey through The Seasons (immersive experience)
events.venue_name: The Westmoreland Museum of American Art
events.description: Journey through the four seasons in this visual exploration of art and nature. In this immersive experience, artworks come alive to celebrate the cycle of life. From darkness, light reveals the birth of a flower, leading into spring and a sense of awakening. Summer brings energy and vitality, followed by the warm, reflective tones of autumn. Winter closes the cycle with stillness and quiet, suggesting contemplation rather than an end. Select paintings from the collection are also on view.

events.description: Shovels & Rope is the Charleston, South Carolina-based husband-and-wife duo of Cary Ann Hearst and Michael Trent. Their music combines folk, country, blues and rock with raw, harmony-driven songwriting and a stripped-down two-person approach. The duo broke through with O’ Be Joyful, which includes the song “Birmingham,” named Song of the Year at the 2013 Americana Music Honors & Awards; Shovels & Rope also received that year’s Emerging Artist award. Their catalog includes Swimmin’ Time, Little Seeds, By Blood and Manticore, showcasing their range from intimate ballads to energetic roots-rock.

events.title: Rhiannon Giddens
events.description: Rhiannon Giddens is a Grammy Award-winning singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist celebrated for her powerful vocals and deep connection to American roots music traditions. Her work blends folk, blues, bluegrass, gospel, jazz, and old-time string music while highlighting the often-overlooked historical contributions of Black musicians to American music. Giddens is widely respected for both her artistry and scholarship, using storytelling and historical themes to create emotionally rich and culturally significant performances. With mastery of instruments like the banjo and fiddle, along with commanding stage presence, Rhiannon Giddens has become one of the most influential voices in contemporary folk and Americana music.

Enjoy antics and laughter galore in this world premiere operatic comedy that gives voice to the unnamed Gentlewoman in Shakespeare’s Macbeth.

events.title: Miss Saigon
events.description: Miss Saigon is a world-renowned musical that combines sweeping romance, unforgettable music, and powerful storytelling to create one of the most emotionally moving productions in modern theater. Featuring music by Claude-Michel Schönberg and lyrics by Alain Boublil and Richard Maltby Jr., the show follows the tragic love story of Kim and Chris against the backdrop of the final days of the Vietnam War and its lasting aftermath. Acclaimed for its soaring score, including memorable songs such as "The Movie in My Mind," "I'd Give My Life for You," and "The American Dream," the production blends intimate character moments with spectacular staging and cinematic theatrical effects. Lavish sets, dynamic choreography, and emotionally charged performances bring the story's themes of sacrifice, hope, love, and resilience vividly to life, making each performance a deeply immersive experience. With its timeless music, compelling characters, and enduring emotional impact, Miss Saigon continues to captivate audiences around the world as one of the most celebrated musicals ever created.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera - Musical
events.description: The Phantom of the Opera is a legendary musical known for its sweeping romance, dramatic storytelling, and unforgettable score composed by Andrew Lloyd Webber. Set beneath the Paris Opera House, the story follows the mysterious Phantom and his obsession with a talented young soprano named Christine. The production is celebrated for iconic songs, elaborate costumes, grand stage effects, and atmospheric set design that create a hauntingly beautiful theatrical experience. As one of the most successful and longest-running musicals in theater history, The Phantom of the Opera continues to captivate audiences around the world.

events.title: Laurie Berkner (Early Show)
events.description: Laurie Berkner is a pioneering children’s recording artist widely associated with the “kindie rock” movement, known for energetic, imaginative songs that appeal to preschool and early elementary-age listeners. She has released bestselling albums including Victor Vito, Rocketship Run, and Under a Shady Tree, and was a featured performer on Nick Jr.’s "Jack’s Big Music Show". Berkner has also performed at Lincoln Center, Carnegie Hall, and the White House, and created the Audible Original series Laurie Berkner’s Song and Story Kitchen.

events.title: MARK NORMAND (Thursday, Early)
events.description: Dubbed by Jerry Seinfeld as the “best young up and coming comic,” Mark Normand is quickly becoming one of the most talked about touring comedians on the scene. Normand’s NEW one- hour Netflix special, SOUP TO NUTS, has been a staple in the streamers’ Top Ten since its July 25th premiere. This follows Normand’s self-released special, 2020’s “Out to Lunch” which amassed over 12 million views on YouTube. He also starred on Netflix’s Season 3 of The Stand Ups. Why'd We Book It? Excited to have the witty Mark Normand joining us this August. Mark is known for his fast talking mixed with puns, one-liners, and quick punchlines which is why we like him. He is quick and to the point, but still keeps a high quality. From podcasts to late night appearances Mark has been in the comedy world for years and has the receipts to back it up. For Fans Of... Gary Gulman, Sam Morrill, Nate Bargatze Extended Bio: An extremely prolific stand-up, he previously had a one-hour and a half hour Comedy Central special and has made an unparalleled seven appearances on “Conan,” four appearances on “The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon,” and has also appeared on “The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.” Mark IS A FREQUENT GUEST ON “The Joe Rogan Experience,” AND HOSTS his own podcasts “Tuesdays with Stories” and “We Might Be Drunk." QR Code Ordering will be available for this performance. Doors open at 5pm. Don't miss our famous Bottlerocket Pre-Show Clip Collection, beginning one hour before the start of the performance. This show is ALL AGES *all information subject to change as needed. Bottlerocket FAQ: All shows starting before 10pm are all ages unless otherwise noted. Free parking is available at 824 Industry Street and 205 Allen Street, as well as other public lots in the area. Live Music shows have limited seating options, please arrive early or reach out to the venue directly if you know that you require a seat. Doors open at 5pm for all shows unless noted otherwise. The time listed on the ticket is the event's true start time. Most shows have a preshow experience starting 1 hour before the show. events.title: Mark Normand
events.description: Mark Normand is a stand-up comedian known for his rapid-fire joke writing, sharp observational humor, and clever takes on everyday social situations. His comedy style blends self-deprecation, wordplay, and quick punchlines, earning him a reputation as one of the most respected joke craftsmen in modern stand-up. Normand has built a devoted following through comedy specials, podcast appearances, and relentless touring, showcasing a comedic voice that is both relatable and refreshingly unfiltered. Known for his energetic delivery and ability to find humor in life's awkward moments, Mark Normand continues to be a standout figure in contemporary comedy.

events.title: Jimmy Failla
events.description: Jimmy Failla is an American stand-up comedian, television host, radio personality, and author known for his fast-paced storytelling, observational humor, and ability to find comedy in everyday life and current events. Before launching his entertainment career, Failla worked as a New York City taxi driver, an experience that provided a wealth of material and helped shape his relatable, quick-witted comedic style. He has performed stand-up at comedy clubs and theaters across the United States while also becoming a familiar media personality through his work on Fox News Radio and as host of the television program Fox News Saturday Night. Failla's comedy blends personal anecdotes, cultural observations, and lighthearted commentary, appealing to audiences with his conversational delivery and approachable stage presence. Whether performing live, broadcasting on radio, or appearing on television, Jimmy Failla has built a reputation as an engaging entertainer whose humor emphasizes shared experiences, clever storytelling, and an infectious sense of fun.

events.title: Jason Ladanye
events.description: The Extraordinary Card Magic of Jason Ladanye brings acclaimed sleight-of-hand performer Jason Ladanye to Pittsburgh for an evening centered on close-up card magic. Known for technically demanding card handling and engaging explanations of his methods, Ladanye has built a large online following and authored the instructional books Confident Deceptions and Game Changer, both recognized within the magic community. His performances transform an ordinary deck into demonstrations of advanced sleight of hand, making this a distinctive live magic presentation rather than a traditional stage illusion show.

events.title: VNV Nation
events.description: VNV Nation is the alternative electronic project led by Dublin-born, Hamburg-based singer, songwriter and producer Ronan Harris. The project is recognized for combining melodic dance beats, indie-electronic anthems, haunting ballads and post-classical textures with thoughtful lyrics. Notable releases include Empires (1999), Noire (2018) and Electric Sun (2023), the latter two reaching No. 4 on the German album chart. VNV Nation’s 2025 album Construct reached No. 3 overall and No. 1 on Germany’s pop-album chart.

events.title: Symposium on 18th Century Living and Customs an Evening with Mrs. Hancock
events.venue_name: The Chapel at Old Main Washington and Jefferson College
events.address: 182 S. Main Street Washington, PA 15301The Chapel at Old Main  Washington & Jefferson College Washington, PA, Washington, Pennsylvania 15301
events.description: The annual history symposium takes place at Old Main, on Washington & Jefferson College.6:30 p.m. — Doors and displays open7 p.m. — Speakers begin9 p.m. — Reception and displaysThe lobby will include:Registration table - check in hereBradford House gift shop table (books)Kate Cunning - cooking demonstrators on the last Saturday of each month in the Bradford House kitchen cabinBryan Cunning - 18th century armory displayOther non-profits to be announced.Admission $40 a person. This is one of the Bradford House Historical Association's annual fundraisers, supporting our mission to educate.Suitable for those 12 years old to 100.Each year, the presenters are chosen based on the period in time they represent and their connection to Southwestern PA.2026 features Mrs. HancockWitness to the Revolution: In April 1775 Dorothy Quincy was engaged to Boston’s wealthiest merchant and Revolutionary Hero, John Hancock. On April 14th she was with her betrothed in Lexington, MA when “the Shot Heard “Round the World” was fired. Newlywed in 1776, Mrs. John Hancock was in Philadelphia serving in an unofficial role as her husband’s secretary when he made his most famous signature on the New Declaration of Independence. When the French Alliance was brokered, it was a resourceful and quick thinking Mrs. Hancock who soothed over matters in Boston in the immediate aftermath of the French Bread Riots of September 1778.As a witness of to the revolution, it seemed Mrs. Hancock was in all the right places at all the right times to tell some of the most interesting tales of American Independence.Kim Hanley: Bio Actor/Historian, Interpreter, Reenactor, Impersonator

events.title: The Outsiders - Musical
events.description: The Outsiders – The Musical brings S.E. Hinton’s classic coming-of-age story to the stage through emotional storytelling, powerful music, and gritty choreography. Set in 1960s Oklahoma, the production follows Ponyboy Curtis and the conflict between the working-class Greasers and the wealthier Socs as they struggle with identity, loyalty, and belonging. The musical combines raw energy with heartfelt performances to capture the emotional depth and timeless themes of friendship, family, and resilience. With its cinematic staging and emotionally driven score, The Outsiders – The Musical reimagines a beloved literary classic for a new generation of theater audiences.

events.title: The Doo Wop Project
events.description: The Doo Wop Project is an acclaimed vocal ensemble that celebrates the timeless harmonies of classic doo-wop while showcasing the evolution of vocal music through energetic performances and contemporary arrangements. Formed by Broadway performers with extensive stage experience, the group combines exceptional vocal talent, polished choreography, and engaging storytelling to honor the music of the 1950s and 1960s while also reimagining modern pop hits in a classic doo-wop style. Audiences can enjoy beloved songs originally made famous by legendary groups alongside inventive renditions of contemporary favorites, all delivered with impeccable harmonies, infectious enthusiasm, and remarkable musical precision. Their concerts seamlessly blend nostalgia, humor, and audience interaction, creating an entertaining experience that appeals to multiple generations of music lovers. With outstanding musicianship, charismatic stage presence, and a genuine passion for preserving the legacy of harmony-driven music, The Doo Wop Project continues to delight audiences with performances that celebrate the enduring power of great songs and unforgettable vocal artistry.

events.title: Clifford the Big Red Dog - The Musical
events.description: Clifford the Big Red Dog – The Musical brings Norman Bridwell's beloved children's classic to the stage in a colorful, family-friendly production filled with music, laughter, and valuable life lessons. The musical follows Clifford and his best friend Emily Elizabeth as they embark on heartwarming adventures that celebrate kindness, friendship, responsibility, and the importance of embracing what makes each individual unique. Featuring lively original songs, engaging choreography, and imaginative sets, the show captures the charm and optimism that have made the giant red dog an enduring favorite for generations of young readers. Families attending the performance can expect an interactive theatrical experience that entertains children while delivering positive messages about compassion, confidence, and working together, making it an enjoyable outing for audiences of all ages.

events.title: The Who's Tommy (Touring)
events.description: The Who’s Tommy is a rock musical based on the groundbreaking album by legendary British band The Who. The story follows Tommy Walker, a boy who retreats into a psychological world of silence and isolation before becoming an unexpected cultural icon through his extraordinary abilities. Known for its explosive rock score, dynamic staging, and emotionally charged performances, the musical blends powerful storytelling with classic songs that helped define rock opera as a genre. With electrifying music, theatrical spectacle, and themes of trauma, healing, and self-discovery, The Who’s Tommy remains one of the most influential rock musicals ever created.

events.title: Whiskey & Spirits Walk
events.address: 182 S. Main Street Washington, PA 15301, Washington, Pennsylvania 15301
events.description: Kick off the Whiskey Rebellion Festival by walking to your favorite local businesses while sampling local spirits.Each business will host vendor-featured distilleries to be announced! Each participant will receive a shot glass. And sold separately is a unique Walk shirt!Friday, July 10, from 6 to 9 pm — $50 per ticketRegistration starts at 5:30 pm at 182 S. Main Street, Washington, Pa 15301 (the Meeting House).Participants are given a wristband, a walking map, and a sampling glass at the Meeting House. The wristband identifies you to the vendors. Spirit and wine vendors are set up throughout the footprint within businesses. You walk from place to place, sampling different libations.If you like something you sample, you can purchase a bottle. Some runners collect all the bottles purchased, and at the end of the walk, you go back to the walk registration and collect your bottles. This way, you don't have to walk around with your bottles. Participants will be given a pretzel snack bag and bottle of water.This is the perfect way to kick off the Whiskey Rebellion Festival!!Participating businesses around town will host a vendor. Walk Map to be shared.Check website shortly for participating distilleries and businesses.

events.title: Whiskey Rebellion Festival
events.description: The Whiskey Rebellion Festival is held by the Bradford House Historical Association.The Whiskey Rebellion Festival honors the significant period of America’s early days through historical reenactments, period exhibitions and demonstrations, family fun, frontier art, heritage music, and food while shining a national spotlight on the city, county, and region. Community-focused entertainment combines nationally renowned artists to create a festival that acknowledges the past, celebrates the present, and look toward the future. The festival always is held the second weekend in July.The festival takes place in downtown Washington, Pa, with a footprint covering the Washington Financial parking lot at Wheeling Street, traveling down Main Street, and ending at Maiden Street. The main events take place on Saturday. The event kicks off with a history parade. The Bradford House, the Whiskey Rebellion Education and Visitor Center and the Meeting House are open for tours during the day on Saturday. And then Saturday concludes with a music headliner.The festival is comprised of:Local history group display tablesBlue Eagle TavernFood trucksHistoric attraction toursLil' Rebels areaMercantile areaMusicReenactorsStreet theatreCourthouse toursProfits go to the BHHA.

events.title: Moraine State Park Regatta
events.description: Join us for a weekend celebrating eco-recreation, community, and the beauty of Moraine State Park. Open on Saturday, August 7th from 10am to 10pm and Sunday, August 8th from 10am to 6pm, the festival is designed to showcase sustainable outdoor fun for visitors of all ages, the annual Regatta offers an action-packed lineup of land and water activities.Whether you're looking to dive into outdoor adventures or relax by the lake, there is something for everyone:- Water Activities: Try your hand at paddleboarding, kayaking, sailing, or cheering on the competitive boat and paddle races across Lake Arthur.- Land Recreation: Participate in organized 5K trail runs, outdoor yoga sessions, guided nature hikes, and disc golf games.- Nature-Themed Experiences: Engage in educational wildlife encounters, interactive conservation workshops, and hands-on environmental activities for kids.- Local Flavor: Explore a bustling marketplace featuring craft vendors, regional food trucks, and live music performance stages.Bring your family, friends, and love for nature to experience everything Moraine State Park has to offer. Admission and parking are free!
